rows.title: the one who comes back
rows.body: your superpower is the return. after the fall, the flood, the year that ate everything, you rebuild with a speed that unsettles people who are still mourning. losing things has never scared you the way it scares others, because some part of you knows the light comes back. it always has.
self_questions: what was your biggest return, and what did it cost?
what would scare you to lose, honestly?

rows.title: laughing at the wound
rows.body: your first response to your own pain is a joke about it. the timing's great, the crowd loves it, and the wound stays exactly where it was. funny buys you distance and it always charges interest.
self_questions: what have you only ever talked about as a bit?

rows.title: early victory energy
rows.body: you celebrate at the start. the announcement, the first day, the leap. beginnings intoxicate you, and you've learned the hard way that middles require a different fuel.
self_questions: which beginning are you proudest of finishing?

rows.title: beauty is a need
rows.body: beauty works on you like weather. the right room, the balanced thing, the lovely arrangement, it changes your actual chemistry. you were built with the sensitivity turned all the way up, and ugly environments genuinely cost you something.
self_questions: what beautiful thing changed your whole state?

rows.title: nobody sees the intense version
rows.body: people might know you as warm or fun. but the real intensity, the fire, the pride, the will, stays where almost nobody gets to go. that's not shyness. the brightest thing you own just doesn't perform.
self_questions: who actually gets to see the intense version of you?
what did you walk away from without ever explaining why? be honest :)

rows.title: the meaningless hour
rows.body: the possibility that none of it means anything visits you at night, and it's not a casual visitor. some of your framework exists specifically to keep that door answered.
self_questions: what do you say when the meaningless hour knocks?

rows.title: the first instinct is the keeper
rows.body: your snap judgment has a better track record than your second-guessing. every time you've overthought your way out of the first answer, you've regretted it. the gut got there first for a reason.
self_questions: when did overthinking talk you out of the right call?

rows.title: security is a number and a feeling
rows.body: your mood quietly tracks your reserves. money set aside calms something old in you, and a dip shows up as dread before you've even done the math.
self_questions: what does enough look like for you?

rows.title: thoughts come in sideways
rows.body: you don't solve problems head on. you circle them, put them down, do the dishes, and the answer walks in uninvited. direct assault never worked on your mind. ambush does.
self_questions: what answer showed up while you were doing something else?

rows.title: the hint isn't a request
rows.body: the mood, the sigh, the hoping they notice. some fights never got fought because the ask never got said out loud, and the resentment got filed as their failure to guess.
self_questions: what have you hinted at that needed saying plainly?

rows.title: keepsakes everywhere
rows.body: you love in objects. the ticket stub, the saved voicemail, the shirt that still smells right. your drawers are archives of affection, and throwing any of it away feels like throwing away the person.
self_questions: what keepsake could you never toss?

rows.title: growth is your native language
rows.body: you grow the way water flows, it's just what you do. new places, new ideas, new bets, all of it feeds you. your faith that things work out is a strategy, and its track record is honestly annoying to more careful people.
self_questions: what worked out on nothing but your faith?

rows.title: more comfort, please
rows.body: your excess runs toward accumulation. the extra, the backup, the just in case. some of what you're storing is security. some of it is just weight wearing security's clothes.
self_questions: what are you keeping that's weight, not safety?

rows.title: exchange is the fuel
rows.body: talking, learning, trading ideas across a table. it literally powers you, and your best days are measured in conversations that went somewhere.
self_questions: what conversation lit you up most recently?

rows.title: it leaks as the empty chair
rows.body: even in full rooms, you notice who's missing. single stretches feel like held breath, and every wedding has a seat that stares back.
self_questions: what does the empty chair say to you?

rows.title: alone is the acquired taste
rows.body: time by yourself takes practice. your default setting is accompanied, and you've quietly built a life where someone's usually near. solitude is a skill you're still learning on purpose.
self_questions: when were you last alone on purpose?

rows.title: ideas stick to people
rows.body: concepts land for you when they're attached to someone. the theory becomes real when it explains your uncle, the strategy makes sense as a story about a founder. abstract floats away. personal stays.
self_questions: what idea finally clicked when it became about a person?

rows.title: you see the lovable in everyone
rows.body: your taste finds the beauty the world overlooked. the awkward one, the faded one, the person nobody photographed. being seen by you has genuinely healed things in people, and some of them never told you.
self_questions: who did you find beautiful that the world missed?

rows.title: the tests
rows.body: you test people without telling them. small ones. how they treat waiters, what they do with a secret, whether they notice you going quiet. most fail. you never mention it.
self_questions: what's the test that matters most, and who passed it?

rows.title: here to transform
rows.body: you're in the metamorphosis business. yours and other people's. you're here to take what's dead or false and compost it into something true, and every chapter of your life has been a demonstration. nothing you touch stays what it was, and that was always the assignment.
self_questions: what have you transformed that no one thought could change?

rows.title: sitting still costs you
rows.body: your leg bounces. you pace on phone calls. people think it's nerves but it's just how you idle. the engine doesn't have an off, only a parked.
self_questions: where does your energy go when there's nowhere to put it?

rows.title: the voice arrives late
rows.body: your speaking confidence came years behind your competence. the person who talks now spent a decade being silent in rooms first, and remembers every one of them.
self_questions: which silent room do you still remember?

rows.title: you teach at the workbench
rows.body: people learn from you by doing the thing next to you, not by hearing you present it. your teaching looks like helping and lands deeper for it. half your students never realized class was in session.
self_questions: who learned the most standing next to you?

rows.title: the pivot is the power
rows.body: you fight adaptively, switching angles mid-move. by the time someone's countered your argument, it's a different argument. pinning you down is the hardest part of opposing you.
self_questions: when did changing angles win it for you?

rows.title: you test before you trust
rows.body: you run quiet tests on people. drop a small thing and watch what they do with it. they never know it was an exam. most of your relationships were decided in moments the other person doesn't remember.
self_questions: what's the last test someone passed without knowing?

rows.title: you learn in pieces
rows.body: your wisdom doesn't come in one big download. it comes in pieces. a podcast here, a conversation there, a question you couldn't let go of. you know a little about everything. that's not scattered. that's how your kind of smart gets built.
self_questions: what's the last rabbit hole you fell down just because?
who do you always help even when nobody asks you to?

rows.title: teachers sense it
rows.body: mentors and sages take to you oddly fast, then run out of things to teach. more than one has looked at you sideways and said some version of you should be up here.
self_questions: which teacher realized you didn't need them?

rows.title: the archive
rows.body: you remember what people said, what they wore, what the weather was doing when it happened. good and bad, all archived. people are shocked at what you can retrieve. forgetting was never one of your talents.
self_questions: what memory do you keep that its other witness lost?

rows.title: the reveal
rows.body: you like a before and after. working in secret, then unveiling the finished thing to gasps. process is private, results are theater.
self_questions: what are you building in secret right now?

rows.title: feelings get explained, not expressed
rows.body: you say i notice some frustration coming up instead of just being frustrated. the translation into analysis happens so fast you rarely catch the raw version. people close to you have felt more of your feelings than you have.
self_questions: what would happen if you skipped the analysis once?

rows.title: rank has costs
rows.body: you're respected more than you're relaxed around. people bring you problems, not gossip, ask your advice, not your company. authority built you a beautiful house with very few doors in.
self_questions: who treats you like a person instead of a position?

rows.title: compliments bounce off
rows.body: someone praises you and you're already listing the flaws they missed. the deflection is instant, almost polite. taking the compliment straight feels like getting away with something.
self_questions: what's a compliment you never let land?

rows.title: growth hides in the ordinary
rows.body: your biggest expansions came from doing a plain thing steadily. the daily practice, the boring consistency, the unglamorous repetition. everyone hunts the exotic door. yours was always the kitchen one.
self_questions: what ordinary practice is secretly your biggest bet?

rows.title: your feelings live in what you make
rows.body: when you're creating something, cooking something, playing, your whole system calms down. your feelings don't live in talk. they live in what your hands are doing. and your heart works the same way. when you love something you really. really. Stay.
self_questions: when was the last time you made something just because it felt good?
what little comfort thing always brings you back to yourself?

rows.title: growth by letting go
rows.body: you expand through surrender, not strategy. the plan released, the grip loosened, the trust in something larger than the spreadsheet. your biggest growth arrived when you stopped forcing, every single time.
self_questions: what grew the moment you stopped forcing it?

rows.title: waiting starves the light
rows.body: queues, committees, permission processes, seasons of hold. your light drops measurably in a holding pattern, and no amount of patience advice has ever changed the physics.
self_questions: what holding pattern is dimming you right now?

rows.title: the architect's burden
rows.body: saturn is home in your sign, and it made your ideals structural. you don't just imagine better systems, you feel responsible for building them. the distance you keep, the discipline of your thinking, the loyalty to principle over mood, it's all the same load, carried well.
self_questions: what better system do you feel responsible for?

rows.title: it leaks as nesting frenzy
rows.body: furniture moved at midnight. eleven tabs of listings for cities you don't live in. the den improved again. the hunger redecorates when it can't relocate.
self_questions: what did you rearrange last, and what were you actually fixing?

rows.title: read as detached in grief
rows.body: your steadiness through loss gets misread as not feeling it. you feel all of it. you've just met death before, and the two of you have an understanding.
self_questions: who needed your grief to be louder?

rows.title: you teach by connecting
rows.body: your gift is the introduction. this person to that one, this idea to that field. whole collaborations exist because you said you two should talk. matchmaking minds is your quiet legacy.
self_questions: which two things did you connect that changed something?

rows.title: protecting can shrink you
rows.body: your excess is over-sheltering. yourself, your people, your possibilities. some of the walls that kept you safe back then are quietly keeping you small right now.
self_questions: which wall finished its job a while ago?

rows.title: luck likes your speed
rows.body: your opportunities have short windows and you catch them because you're already moving. the door that closed on everyone else was open when you got there. the only expensive thing you've ever done is hesitate.
self_questions: what did you catch because you moved first?

rows.title: the connoisseur's heart
rows.body: your love runs through the senses. texture, taste, weight, the smell of the real thing. you love slowly and thoroughly, in full physicality, and anything worth loving is worth experiencing at quarter speed.
self_questions: what do you love slowly that others rush?

rows.title: already someone
rows.body: the self everyone else is busy building, you arrived with. you've never really performed an identity, never rebranded, never needed the room to tell you who you are. it puzzles people. it bores you. you finished that assignment before this life started.
self_questions: when did you first notice you weren't searching for yourself?

rows.title: the first responder
rows.body: something in you moves toward the hurt thing before you've decided to. a friend texts bad news and you're already typing, already fixing, already halfway there. you soothe fast and you start fast. the hard part is staying past the rescue, when there's nothing left to fix and someone just wants you to sit there.
self_questions: who taught you that helping fast was the same as loving?
what happens if you arrive and just stay?

rows.title: the mood wears you
rows.body: your feelings show up in your whole body. posture, face, the plans for the day, all of it runs on your current mood. people can read your state from across the street, and honestly the street can too.
self_questions: what mood are you wearing today?

rows.title: you learn by performing it
rows.body: the material becomes yours when you present it. explaining to the room, teaching the junior, holding forth at dinner. before the performance, it's notes. after, it's knowledge.
self_questions: what did you finally understand by teaching it?

rows.title: 2am browsing
rows.body: apartments in cities you don't live in. courses you won't take. flights you won't book. your search history is a map of a hundred lives you're keeping warm.
self_questions: which of those other lives keeps coming back?

rows.title: tender is the taste
rows.body: you love what feels like home. the worn-in, the sentimental, the person who remembers what you said in passing. new and shiny has never once beaten old and meaningful in your heart's rankings.
self_questions: what do you love because of what it remembers?

rows.title: the kind knife
rows.body: your love has an edge. you feed people, protect them, show up with soup and hard truths in the same bag. you'd rather hurt someone with honesty than comfort them with a lie, and you've lost a few people who wanted the lie. the ones who stayed trust you more than anyone.
self_questions: who in your life can handle your full honesty?
when has softness actually been the truer move?

rows.title: you think by arguing
rows.body: your ideas get sharp through friction. a good debate clarifies your position better than an hour of quiet reflection ever could. people who agree with everything you say are pleasant and completely useless to your process.
self_questions: who's your favorite person to argue with?

rows.title: you meet people at their worst
rows.body: you understand people best when they're breaking. polished versions bore you slightly. show you someone mid storm and you finally know who they are.
self_questions: who has seen you mid storm, and what did they learn?

rows.title: done means done
rows.body: when you decide you're finished with something, there's no announcement. no big talk. the door just closes and you don't look back. people sometimes find out months later.
self_questions: what did you walk away from without ever explaining why?

rows.title: the hearth
rows.body: where you are becomes where it's happening. people gather around you the way they gather around fires, without deciding to. being the center is your function, and the gathering is the proof it's working.
self_questions: where do people gather because you're there?

rows.title: depth charges you
rows.body: real conversations, real stakes, truth with its coat off. intensity is your actual food source, and a week of depth restores you more than a month of pleasant ever has.
self_questions: what deep thing fed you recently?

rows.title: applause has a half-life
rows.body: the win feels incredible for about a day. then the silence after it is louder than the silence before. the dose keeps needing to grow, and the pharmacy keeps raising prices.
self_questions: how long did the last big moment last?

rows.title: the long game in every plan
rows.body: you think in decades by default. today's choice gets evaluated against a version of you that's twenty years out, and that meeting has vetoed a lot of fun. it's also why your life compounds while others' resets.
self_questions: what are you doing now that's really for the you of 2040?

rows.title: the cold front
rows.body: controlled anger reads as glacier. people around you can't repair what you won't show is broken, and some things stayed broken for years behind the perfect composure.
self_questions: what's broken behind the composure?

rows.title: pointlessness dims you
rows.body: busywork, broken systems nobody lets you fix, effort that serves no one you can name. your light doesn't dim from hard work. it dims from work that lands nowhere.
self_questions: what effort of yours is landing nowhere?

rows.title: nothing to hold dims you
rows.body: stretches with no one and nothing in your care leave you dimmer than exhaustion ever has. your light needs somewhere to point. empty-handed seasons are your hardest kind.
self_questions: what could you take into your care right now?

rows.title: perfect timing
rows.body: you arrive, text, launch, and leave at the exactly right moment, by feel. people plan what you just sense. your calendar is a metronome only you can hear.
self_questions: when has your timing saved you?

rows.title: the grind is the identity
rows.body: exhaustion reads as evidence. rest feels like losing ground to someone, somewhere, who didn't stop. the tired became part of the uniform so long ago you forgot it comes off.
self_questions: what would it mean about you if you rested?

rows.title: read as somewhere else
rows.body: people tell you that you seem far away, and you are. the far away is load bearing. you always come back, and you come back better, and they've mostly stopped worrying.
self_questions: where's the far away you go to?

rows.title: nothing to prove out loud
rows.body: you've never needed the last word. arguments other people would die on, you just leave, and the leaving costs you nothing. the courage everyone performs, you spend quietly. you already know what you think, and needing it heard finished before you got here.
self_questions: what argument did you walk away from that others couldn't?

rows.title: the involuntary critic
rows.body: you notice the crooked frame from across the room. the kerning, the seam, the wrong word in the toast. you've learned to not say most of it. the noticing never stops though.
self_questions: what do you wish you could stop noticing?

rows.title: space is oxygen
rows.body: you can love someone completely and still need them to leave for a while. distance doesn't mean anything's wrong, it's how you stay breathable. the people who last are the ones who never made you explain it.
self_questions: who loves you without crowding you?

rows.title: aimlessness dims you
rows.body: no mountain, no mission, and your light drops fast. rest without direction reads as fog to your system. you don't need less work to get bright. you need truer work.
self_questions: when did aimlessness last dim you, and what re-aimed you?

rows.title: growth you can stand on
rows.body: your expansion is structural. the title earned, the thing built, the position that took a decade. luck, for you, looks suspiciously like work, and abundance arrives as authority. what you grow doesn't wilt.
self_questions: what did you build that you now stand on?

rows.title: the double life
rows.body: there's the you at work and the 2am you, and the gap is bigger than anyone guesses. it's not deception. it's that most rooms can't hold the whole voltage.
self_questions: which room gets the most of you?

rows.title: love letters, all day
rows.body: your affection lives in the running exchange. the meme that says i thought of you, the link, the voice note, the thread that never closes. your love language has a keyboard, and it's fluent.
self_questions: who's in the exchange that never ends?

rows.title: worth got tangled with wallet
rows.body: a bad money month feels like a character verdict. the account balance and the self balance got wired together somewhere back there, and every dip reads as a judgment.
self_questions: when did money start grading you?

rows.title: the trained intensity
rows.body: your control is built. the emotional composure, the strategic patience, the steady face under real pressure, all constructed through years that demanded them daily. nothing about your calm is luck.
self_questions: what years built your composure?

rows.title: the hundred healers
rows.body: you heal in unconventional ways, and you do it behind a veil. your methods, your privacy, your strange solitary practices, none of it looks like what it does. people find you mysterious because you are: a circle with a hundred remedies inside and one small guarded entrance. you can fix what others can't. the person you struggle most to treat is the one running the pharmacy.
self_questions: what's your strangest remedy that actually works?
who's allowed inside the circle?

rows.title: you feel the undercurrent
rows.body: every room has a surface conversation and a real one, and you're tuned to the real one. unspoken tension reaches you like a smell. small talk has never once fooled you.
self_questions: what's the real conversation in the room lately?

rows.title: feelings at arm's length
rows.body: you understand your emotions better than you feel them. something happens and you're already narrating from the ceiling, curious, a little detached, taking notes. it keeps you calm in every crisis. it also means some feelings wait years for their turn.
self_questions: what have you understood completely but never actually felt?

rows.title: slow explanations hurt
rows.body: you finish people's sentences in your head, and sometimes out loud. meandering stories, buried points, wind-ups with no pitch, all of it costs you real effort to sit through. patience with slow talkers is your most practiced skill.
self_questions: who do you love that you wish would get to the point?

rows.title: calm in chaos
rows.body: everyone panicking, plans collapsing, and you go strangely still. crisis focuses you. it's the quiet normal days that make you feel unqualified.
self_questions: what would it mean to be good at ordinary days too?

rows.title: build past your own name
rows.body: fed right, this hunger leaves real things standing. institutions, works, doors held open for people climbing behind you. aim it past your own name, and it finally, mercifully, quiets.
self_questions: what could you build that outlives the title?

rows.title: the seeking is the faith
rows.body: fed right, this hunger is a real spiritual life, not a shopping problem. the truth you're starving for behaves more like a direction than a possession, and you've been walking it the whole time.
self_questions: what if you're already on the path you're searching for?

rows.title: zoomed out past your own feet
rows.body: you can explain the decade's trajectory and miss what's in front of you. keys, appointments, the thing they literally just said. the horizon has your full attention, and the foreground pays for it.
self_questions: what nearby thing are you missing while watching the horizon?

rows.title: growth by shedding
rows.body: your expansions require a death first. the identity, the relationship, the story that had to end before the next size of you could start. you grow like a snake, whole skins at a time.
self_questions: what skin are you in the middle of shedding?

rows.title: focused looks like angry on you
rows.body: people keep asking if you're ok when you're just concentrating. resting intensity. you're usually fine. you're usually just locked in on something.
self_questions: who reads you wrong the most?

rows.title: the numbers whisper
rows.body: metrics check themselves through your thumbs. followers, views, rsvps, the counts stand in for belonging, and belonging keeps not arriving by count.
self_questions: which number do you check without deciding to?

rows.title: cynicism dims you
rows.body: rooms that sneer at meaning, seasons of small talk about small things, the fashionable nothing-matters. your light needs sky, and cynical air has none in it.
self_questions: what cynical room do you need to leave?

rows.title: crying is a private event
rows.body: your tears have an audience limit of about one, and usually zero. you'll hold it together through the funeral and fall apart in the car. vulnerability happens on your terms, in your spaces, on your schedule.
self_questions: where do you go to fall apart?

rows.title: the buried charge
rows.body: anger you bury doesn't die down there, it mines. some of your detonations were years in the digging, and the people caught in them only ever saw the last day.
self_questions: what's still buried that's still digging?

rows.title: will, built by hand
rows.body: your drive was assembled rep by rep. nobody handed you momentum, so you built the engine while driving it. what looks like natural push is actually maintained machinery.
self_questions: when did you first realize you'd built your own drive?

rows.title: decisions need a deadline
rows.body: without a forcing function, your weighing runs forever. the restaurant, the job offer, the font. you decide beautifully under pressure and endlessly without it. the deadline is your best thinking partner.
self_questions: what decision needs a deadline right now?

rows.title: the long-distance heart
rows.body: your closest people are scattered across time zones and you keep every thread alive. voice notes, odd-hour calls, the friendship maintained across nine years and three countries. distance never once meant less to you.
self_questions: which faraway person feels closest?

rows.title: vision charges you
rows.body: possibility, better designs, the improved version of anything. thinking about what could be generates your energy the way memory generates other people's. the future is your power source, and it never runs out.
self_questions: what possibility is currently powering you?

rows.title: you feel the shift before the words
rows.body: you know something's off with your people before they say a thing. a text with different punctuation, a pause one beat too long. lying to you is basically pointless and everyone close to you learns that.
self_questions: what shift are you sensing right now that nobody's named?

rows.title: wanting gripped too hard
rows.body: the intensity has closed its hand before. wanting someone and watching them blurred once or twice, and you didn't love who you were inside it. desire that deep needs an open palm, and the palm took practice.
self_questions: when did wanting turn into holding too tight?

rows.title: the fast conclusion
rows.body: your mind gets to the point before most people finish the sentence. decisions that take others weeks take you minutes, and you're right often enough to trust it. thinking, for you, is a sprint with an answer at the end.
self_questions: what did you decide instantly that turned out right?

rows.title: comfortable in ruins
rows.body: other people's rock bottom is your working altitude. loss, endings, the dismantled life. you're strangely calm there, because at the bottom there's finally nothing left to lose or fake.
self_questions: what did you find at your bottom that you still use?

rows.title: the reinvention loop
rows.body: new look, new city, new name energy. the self keeps getting rebuilt, and each version was quietly supposed to be the one. the construction never closes.
self_questions: which version of you was supposed to be final?

rows.title: the other shore
rows.body: you think about elsewhere a lot, the sea, the next life chapter, the world past this one. endings don't frighten you the way they frighten others. you've always sensed a far shore.
self_questions: what does your far shore look like?

rows.title: discipline is the weapon
rows.body: you outwork opposition. talent, charisma, connections, all of it loses to your calendar eventually. showing up daily is your violence, and it's undefeated.
self_questions: what did your consistency beat that talent couldn't?

rows.title: the eldest
rows.body: whether or not you were born first, you became the eldest. the one who handles it, holds the keys, gets the call when it all goes wrong. protection is your instinct and burden is its price, and you've carried responsibility so long it feels like posture now. the part nobody sees: how much you'd give for someone to occasionally check on the protector.
self_questions: who protects the protector?
what would you put down if you believed someone else would catch it?

rows.title: the mountain remembers
rows.body: every load you've carried built the person who can carry more, and by the last stretch you're the one others rope themselves to. that was always the deal. it was always worth it.
self_questions: who's roped to you on the climb?

rows.title: brave on the outside first
rows.body: the trick nobody clocks is that you look fearless before you feel it. you say yes, then your stomach catches up. honestly, it works. the body goes first and the courage follows it in.
self_questions: what did you say yes to before you were ready?

rows.title: truth as comfort
rows.body: when someone spirals, you don't say it'll be okay. you say what's actually happening, plainly, and somehow that calms them more than softness would.
self_questions: who calms you down, and how do they do it?

rows.title: planted can mean stuck
rows.body: the same feet that make you immovable in a fight sometimes hold you in place past the point of sense. leaving anything takes you seasons, even the things on fire.
self_questions: where are you planted that you should be walking?

rows.title: the perfection lesson
rows.body: saturn doubled your editor. good enough was never in the vocabulary, error felt expensive from the start, and your standards have run your life like a strict landlord. the lesson, arriving slowly, is that done teaches more than perfect ever did.
self_questions: what did shipping something imperfect finally teach you?

rows.title: the unfinished argument
rows.body: you draft comebacks in the shower. you win conversations that ended years ago, nightly. the courtroom in your head has never once adjourned.
self_questions: which argument are you still winning alone?

rows.title: final on purpose
rows.body: your decisions age well because you make them slowly and mean them completely. people have learned not to relitigate with you. when you say it's settled, the matter has a tombstone.
self_questions: what settled decision quietly shaped everything after it?

rows.title: hungry for the truth
rows.body: you're starving for the answer. the philosophy, the teacher, the framework that finally explains all of it. you've believed hard, unbelieved harder, and packed for every pilgrimage. the question mark is the hungriest shape you know.
self_questions: what question has driven the whole search?

rows.title: bored by the current version
rows.body: your interest lives one iteration ahead. today's tools, today's debates, today's setup, all mildly stale, because you've already moved into what's next. the present keeps having to catch up to where you've been waiting.
self_questions: what are you early to this time?

rows.title: the compromised ideal
rows.body: selling out, watering down, becoming the thing you critiqued. that fear holds veto power over your choices, and it has used the veto more than anyone knows.
self_questions: what did the fear of selling out veto?

rows.title: the mirror never confirms
rows.body: no reflection, no milestone, no compliment has ever said arrived. you hit the goal and the goalposts breathe. the confirmation you're starving for doesn't come from where you keep looking.
self_questions: what did you become that still wasn't it?

rows.title: the summit doesn't call
rows.body: ambition never stuck to you. titles, ladders, the view from the top everyone's bleeding for, you can see it clearly and feel nothing. you'll do excellent work and walk away from the promotion. careers happen to you sideways, while you're busy with what actually matters.
self_questions: what promotion did you walk away from without a wound?

rows.title: trust issues with delegation
rows.body: you'd rather do it yourself than watch someone do it worse. it's faster, it's cleaner, and it's slowly burying you. help exists. you've just never fully believed in it.
self_questions: what would you hand off if you trusted the hands?

rows.title: the fast healer
rows.body: you get over things suspiciously fast. sick for a day, heartbroken for a week, back on your feet before anyone finished worrying. sometimes you wonder if you healed or just outran it.
self_questions: is there something you moved past that never actually closed?

rows.title: your mind is the sharpest thing you own
rows.body: big ideas, beliefs, how everything connects. you don't just learn things, you kind of fall in love with them. it's a real gift and it has a real price. the same mind that sees the structure in everything sees the flaws in everything too. including people.
self_questions: what idea or subject are you a little bit in love with right now?
be honest. do you critique the people you love more than they know?

rows.title: craft over charisma
rows.body: you built skill where others coasted on sparkle. rehearsed, structured, earned. your confidence is made of work, and work doesn't have off nights the way sparkle does.
self_questions: what craft carries you where charisma carries others?

rows.title: luck comes through kin
rows.body: your doors open through family, through people who treat you like family, through the friend of your mother's friend. blood and chosen blood are your network, and it's warmer than any linkedin.
self_questions: which door opened through someone who loves you?

rows.title: who gets the real you
rows.body: most people get the warm version. a few get glimpses. the full intensity has maybe been seen by two or three people ever. that's not a wall. it's a door, and you hold the key."
self_questions: when did you last let someone all the way in?

rows.title: the ceiling called realistic
rows.body: your excess is caution dressed as wisdom. some dreams got pre-shrunk to fit the plan before they ever got a chance to be measured. realistic has occasionally been fear with a spreadsheet.
self_questions: what dream did you shrink before trying it at full size?

rows.title: bored feels like sad
rows.body: you've mistaken understimulation for depression more than once. sometimes the heavy gray feeling lifts the second something interesting walks in. your mind needs feeding on a schedule, and hunger there feels like grief.
self_questions: when did boredom last disguise itself as something darker?

rows.title: drawn to the laugh
rows.body: humor is your beauty standard, full stop. the funny plain person beats the gorgeous bore forever, in every category, at every age. if they can't make you laugh, they never had a chance.
self_questions: who won you entirely by being funny?

rows.title: comfort isn't extra
rows.body: good food. soft things. the same show for the fourth time. some people treat comfort like a guilty pleasure. for you it's how you stay okay. you run on it.
self_questions: what's your most reliable little comfort?

rows.title: the unshockable
rows.body: people preface confessions with you're going to judge me, and you never do. you've seen far enough into yourself that nothing human surprises you anymore.
self_questions: what did you find in yourself that ended your ability to judge?

rows.title: the need announces itself
rows.body: you always know what you need. rest, food, space, out. the knowing is instant and loud. the asking is a whole different skill, and it came with no manual.
self_questions: what do you need right now?

rows.title: the goal keeps you steady
rows.body: having something to aim at regulates you. when there's no active target, your feelings drift and go sour. the goal was never just ambition. it's emotional infrastructure.
self_questions: what are you aiming at right now?

rows.title: greyness dims the light
rows.body: the joyless job, the beige season, the calendar with no occasion in it anywhere. your light needs celebration the way lungs need air, and austerity has never once made you better.
self_questions: where has the grey crept in?

rows.title: the group chat is a coping tool
rows.body: your daily feelings get metabolized in running conversations. memes as check-ins, jokes as care, the thread that never really ends. it looks like chatter. it's maintenance.
self_questions: which chat holds your day?

rows.title: patience like a weapon
rows.body: you can wait longer than anyone. not passive waiting, coiled waiting. people forget what you said you'd do. you don't. years later you arrive exactly where you pointed.
self_questions: what are you currently waiting out?

rows.title: growth in the giving away
rows.body: your expansions follow generosity. what you release comes back grown, and the tightest years of your life were the ones you held on hardest. your hands work best open, in every direction.
self_questions: what would opening your hands release right now?

rows.title: the sudden shed
rows.body: you can hold on for years past reason, then leave in one night, whole, final, like a skin left on the road. the people you leave never see it coming. you'd been leaving for months.
self_questions: when did your last leaving actually begin?

rows.title: making things calms you down
rows.body: loud head? you cook. restless? you build, sort, fix, play. it looks like productivity from the outside. it's actually how you settle. your hands know the way back.
self_questions: what do you make when you need to come back to yourself?

rows.title: mastery over sampling
rows.body: you'd rather know one thing completely than ten things adequately. the deep single track suits you, the buffet doesn't. being merely conversant in something you care about feels like a debt.
self_questions: what's the one thing you're going all the way down on?

rows.title: anxiety is the alarm system
rows.body: your mind runs safety checks on everything you care about. the more you love something, the louder the checking gets. it's exhausting, and it's also just what guarding treasure sounds like from the inside.
self_questions: what does your worry guard?

rows.title: solitude is the residence
rows.body: alone isn't a state you visit. it's the address, and company is the excursion. you were never lonely there, whatever anyone assumed.
self_questions: what happens in your solitude that nobody's ever seen?

rows.title: the escape hatch
rows.body: you need somewhere else to go. sleep, water, music, fiction, the inside of your own head. checking out is sometimes just maintenance. a heart that open needs a back room.
self_questions: where's your somewhere else?

rows.title: the crusade
rows.body: your drive needs a banner. you fight magnificently for beliefs, causes, the big right thing, and barely at all for small personal stakes. your anger is loud, philosophical, and over quickly. a thunderstorm with opinions.
self_questions: what banner gets your whole fire?

rows.title: the healer's exemption
rows.body: free of the race, your hands are open to actually tend things. people, systems, bodies, whatever's broken nearby. fixing without competing is a whole vocation, and it might be the one with your name on it.
self_questions: what could you tend if winning was fully off the table?

rows.title: the bridge
rows.body: your role is being the one both sides trust. agreements exist because you stood in the middle and held. whole relationships, deals, and families function because you were the span between them.
self_questions: which two sides trust you at once?

rows.title: people exhale around you
rows.body: you're the friend people call when everything's on fire, just to hear a voice that isn't. you don't even do anything special. you just don't panic, and the room borrows it.
self_questions: who comes to you to calm down?

rows.title: celebration deficit
rows.body: you hit the goal and feel it for about an hour. then the eye moves to the next ridge. your wins pile up uncelebrated, which is efficient and a little sad.
self_questions: what win deserves the party you never threw it?

rows.title: compliments land strangely
rows.body: praise about who you are slides off, and never from modesty. it's information about a topic you closed a long time ago. you say thank you and change the subject, every time.
self_questions: what compliment can you genuinely not absorb?

rows.title: feeding as speech
rows.body: you say i love you in portions. extra servings, packed leftovers, remembering exactly what someone can't eat. the table is where you actually talk.
self_questions: what meal says the most about how you love?

rows.title: belief arrives late and solid
rows.body: your real convictions came after the borrowed ones collapsed, and the collapse took years you remember clearly. what you believe now, you could defend under oath, alone, unprepared.
self_questions: which borrowed belief had to collapse first?

rows.title: drawn to competence
rows.body: skill is your aphrodisiac. watching someone be genuinely good at something, the sure hands, the economy of motion. mastery does more for you than beauty ever managed.
self_questions: whose skill made them attractive to you?

rows.title: the group's quiet glue
rows.body: every group you're in holds together partly because of maintenance you do invisibly. the check-ins, the remembering, the bridge repairs after fights. nobody assigned you this. you'd never resign.
self_questions: what would your groups lose if you stopped tending them for a month?

rows.title: the door opens inward
rows.body: fed right, this hunger is mystical, full stop. meditation, art, service, the ocean, the states that dissolve you and hand you back bigger. the release you're starving for exists. it just isn't behind any of the exits.
self_questions: what dissolves you and gives you back more?

rows.title: three real ones
rows.body: your loyalty runs vertical, not horizontal. few people, full depth, decades long. the roster hasn't changed in years and the door isn't broken, it's just satisfied.
self_questions: who are your three?

rows.title: softness arrives late
rows.body: your ease with your own feelings came years in. the person who can cry now, say the tender thing now, spent a long time learning it was allowed. it was always allowed. the learning was the hard part.
self_questions: what tenderness took you years to permit yourself?

rows.title: clean fire
rows.body: your drive is direct and honest. you want, you go, you say it to their face. anger comes fast, burns clean, leaves no smoke. people always know where they stand with your fire, which is rarer than it sounds.
self_questions: who respects your fire because it's honest?

rows.title: the friend in exile
rows.body: you bloom far from home. your deepest friendships were made in foreign places, hard seasons, groups you weren't born into, because devotion is your gift and it works anywhere. you know how to love people through distance, difference, and years of silence. what you're worse at is believing you're loved back with the same weight. you keep quietly earning what was already yours.
self_questions: which friendship proved you could be at home anywhere?
who loves you at full weight that you keep half doubting?

rows.title: the safe passage
rows.body: you're the last nakshatra, the shepherd at the end of the road, and it shows: lost things find you. lost people, lost animals, travelers, the friend mid crisis at your door. you guide things home, often at your own expense, because abandoning anyone anywhere feels physically impossible to you. your sweetness is not naivety. it's a choice you keep making in a world that keeps testing it.
self_questions: who did you guide home at cost to yourself?
where is your own home, the one someone would guide you to?

rows.title: the invigorator
rows.body: tired rooms wake up when you enter. you carry a current, and people near you start believing their own plans again. you rarely notice you're doing it.
self_questions: who do you recharge, and who recharges you?

rows.title: show me beats tell me
rows.body: theory slides off you. a demonstration sticks. you trust what you've seen work with your own eyes over any amount of explanation, and you're usually right to.
self_questions: what did you refuse to believe until you saw it?

rows.title: anger goes analytical
rows.body: you get mad in theories. the rant arrives as a lecture with citations, a systems critique with a reading list. your fury has never once been unstructured.
self_questions: what's your current furious thesis?

rows.title: moods come in tides
rows.body: some days the water's just high and there's no reason to find. you used to hunt for explanations. now you know some moods are tidal, they roll in, they roll out, and needing a cause is optional.
self_questions: what helps you wait out a high tide?

rows.title: effortless you
rows.body: you don't practice being yourself. no mirror pep talks, no personal brand, no curated angles. what others construct daily, you just wear.
self_questions: what do people work at that comes free to you?

rows.title: learning as breathing
rows.body: you're always in the middle of learning something. a language, a history, a rabbit hole at 1am. your mind is a student who never once considered graduating.
self_questions: what are you secretly studying right now?

rows.title: drawn to substance
rows.body: you're attracted to accomplishment worn quietly. the person who does what they said, the track record, the competence that doesn't advertise. potential is cute. delivered is beautiful.
self_questions: whose reliability became attractive over time?

rows.title: growth through belonging
rows.body: you expand where you're rooted. family, home, the people who are yours. your biggest growth never came from leaving, it came from deepening. you build the nest bigger and the nest builds you back.
self_questions: where are you most rooted, and what has grown there?

rows.title: the gate opens slowly
rows.body: your affection has a vetting period, and the vetting has outlasted some applicants worth keeping. a few good ones aged out of the queue waiting for a yes you were always going to give.
self_questions: who aged out of your queue that you still think about?

rows.title: strange beauty
rows.body: your taste runs contrary. drawn to the odd, the original, the thing nobody else at the table would pick. conventional pretty bores you at a cellular level, and your favorites have always needed explaining.
self_questions: what do you love that you always have to explain?

rows.title: the point, then maybe the footnotes
rows.body: you get the essence of the book from the introduction and the reviews. fine print, terms, appendices, all skipped on principle. it costs you occasionally and saves you years cumulatively.
self_questions: what fine print should you probably have read?

rows.title: the fast rebuild
rows.body: when things collapse you're already sketching the next version. friends worry you haven't grieved. you have. you just do it while moving.
self_questions: is there a collapse you rebuilt over instead of through?

rows.title: it leaks as scorekeeping
rows.body: who got credited, who's ahead, whose output. the leaderboard in your head refreshes hourly, and it has never once shown you in first for longer than a morning.
self_questions: what score are you tracking today?

rows.title: the why under the why
rows.body: someone gives you a reason and you hear the reason under it. you keep asking until you hit bedrock. therapists love you or fear you, there's no third option.
self_questions: what's your bedrock why, the one under all your others?

rows.title: the quest charges you
rows.body: journeys, questions, the next understanding just past the current one. seeking is your metabolism. you don't recover by stopping. you recover by pointing somewhere new.
self_questions: what quest is currently keeping you alive?

rows.title: you edit while you love
rows.body: sometimes you notice every little flaw in someone before your heart even gets a say. the noticing is automatic. what you do with it is the choice. the people worth keeping are the ones you can stop proofreading around.
self_questions: be honest. do you critique the people you love more than they know?

rows.title: hungry for the top
rows.body: you're starving for the summit. the title, the name that opens rooms, the view from undeniable. you've spent evenings, years, softer versions of your life on the climb. and every peak you've reached had another one behind it, smirking.
self_questions: which summit was supposed to be the last one?

rows.title: the mind builds
rows.body: your thinking is architecture. foundation first, one idea stacked on the last, nothing decorative. you're slower to answer than the quick minds in the room, and ten years later your answer is the one still standing.
self_questions: what conclusion of yours has outlasted everyone's hot takes?

rows.title: touch and food
rows.body: your love language is embarrassingly physical. feeding people, hugging a beat too long, fixing someone's collar. words are fine but they're not proof. proof is warm and edible.
self_questions: how do you know when someone actually loves you?

rows.title: the sideways fighter
rows.body: your drive moves like a crab. indirect, armored, and absolutely getting there. you fight hardest for your people and rarely for yourself, and your anger comes out at angles: the mood, the withdrawal, the door closed slightly harder than necessary.
self_questions: what does your anger look like to someone who knows you?

rows.title: the persuasion current
rows.body: you don't argue, you flow. by the end of the conversation people have somehow moved to where you're standing and believe they walked there themselves.
self_questions: who's the one person you've never been able to move?

rows.title: the face gives nothing
rows.body: your best poker face isn't for cards. it's for the moment someone tells you something huge and you just nod. people trust you with bombs because you don't flinch when they hand them over.
self_questions: what secret have you kept so well the teller forgot you know it?

rows.title: looking fine isn't being fine
rows.body: the composed face is automatic. it goes on before you decide anything. which means you can be struggling and nobody knows, because you look exactly the same. the face is a skill. it's also a hiding place.
self_questions: when did you last look fine and not be fine?

rows.title: form arrives late
rows.body: the container for your gifts came years after the gifts themselves. the talent was always there, whole. the discipline that ships it was built in adulthood, plank by plank, and it's still being built.
self_questions: what talent waited years for its container?

rows.title: lit means building it together
rows.body: at full vitality, the vision has a crew. the future is a group project, and your brightest state is architect among builders, not prophet alone on the hill. find the hands. the blueprint deserves them.
self_questions: who belongs on your crew?

rows.title: the outfit is the argument
rows.body: how a thing looks is part of what it means, and you've never understood people who pretend otherwise. you dress like it matters because to you it genuinely does.
self_questions: what does your favorite outfit say that you don't say out loud?

rows.title: the earned shine
rows.body: saturn sits on your light. being seen, taking the stage, believing you deserve the room's attention, none of it came easy, and you've dimmed yourself in rooms that deserved your full wattage. the shine you carry now was earned against gravity. that's why it doesn't flicker.
self_questions: where did you used to dim yourself?

rows.title: the past holds the menu
rows.body: you keep loving what loved you first. the childhood dish, the old song, the familiar face. new tastes have to fight your entire history for a seat at the table, and most of them lose.
self_questions: what new thing deserves a fair fight against your past?

rows.title: drawn to the flame
rows.body: confidence is your beauty standard. the person who takes up space, says the thing, walks in first. courage reads as gorgeous to you, and hesitation has never once been attractive.
self_questions: whose boldness caught you?

rows.title: a mirror with good manners
rows.body: you reflect people back at themselves slightly improved. their jokes land better around you, their stories sound smarter. it's a gift. it also means some people love your company without knowing you at all.
self_questions: who loves being around you without knowing you?

rows.title: the summit alone
rows.body: the higher you climb, the fewer people can follow, and lately the view is beautiful and quiet. achievement has been thinning your company for years. you noticed. you climbed anyway.
self_questions: who do you want beside you at the top?

rows.title: beauty is the spark
rows.body: you love things at first sight or not at all. the pull is instant, physical, undeniable, and it has never once needed a second look to decide. you're drawn to the bold, the direct, the alive, and your taste has the reflexes of a struck match.
self_questions: what did you love the instant you saw it?

rows.title: the medicine hunter
rows.body: you're drawn to what heals at the root, not the symptom. real answers, hard practices, medicine that tastes like truth. comfort that doesn't cure has never interested you.
self_questions: what actually healed you versus what just soothed you?

rows.title: light that holds
rows.body: because your shine was built, it survives criticism, bad nights, empty rooms. borrowed confidence flickers at the first draft of wind. yours is wired into the walls.
self_questions: what storm did your confidence survive that would have killed the borrowed kind?

rows.title: the native load
rows.body: saturn is home in your sign, and the weight has always felt familiar. responsibility finds you, structures obey you, the long climb is your natural gait. you never needed the lesson explained. you were born mid-semester, already carrying, already fluent.
self_questions: what have you carried so long it feels like posture?

rows.title: you carry the room home
rows.body: you leave gatherings tired in a very specific way. it's everyone else's moods, packed and taken with you like a coat grabbed by mistake. hours later you're sad and can't source it. it was never yours.
self_questions: whose mood are you wearing right now?

rows.title: faith without the manual
rows.body: you never needed the guru. doctrines, scriptures, the frameworks people climb like ladders, you skimmed and set down. something in you already knows, wordlessly, and the knowing predates every book on the shelf. belief systems read like maps of a town you grew up in.
self_questions: what have you always known without being taught?

rows.title: letting go takes years
rows.body: you hold on past the expiration date. relationships, grudges, sweaters, versions of your life that already ended. the grip is loyal and it's also heavy. some things you're still carrying were over long ago.
self_questions: what ended a while ago that you're still holding?

rows.title: you can dim on purpose
rows.body: when you're done being perceived you just fade. still in the room, somehow not in it, and people's eyes slide past. presence has a dial on you and you're the only one who knows where it is.
self_questions: when did you last dim on purpose?

rows.title: hungry for the multitude
rows.body: you're starving for the big room. the network, the movement, the win with many zeroes and many witnesses. one friend, one sale, one like was never the appetite. you want reach, and reach keeps redefining itself upward.
self_questions: how big would the room have to be?

rows.title: all-in pursuit
rows.body: when you want something, your whole life reorganizes around it, invisibly. the routines, the choices, the hours, all quietly redirected. people call your results luck because they never saw the machine.
self_questions: what are you all-in on that nobody's noticed?

rows.title: the mirror teaches
rows.body: fed right, this hunger makes you a master of partnership. every relationship handed you a missing piece of yourself, and the collection is nearly complete. the next one gets a whole person.
self_questions: what piece did the last one hand you?

rows.title: you learn from people, not pages
rows.body: a subject opens up when a person you trust walks you through it. the same material in a cold pdf just sits there. warmth is part of your bandwidth, and the best things you know came from someone's voice.
self_questions: who taught you the things you actually use?

rows.title: hungry for enough
rows.body: there's a hunger in you around worth. money, security, being valued. no matter how much you have, some part of you keeps checking if it's enough. the hunger is real. the numbers were never going to feed it.
self_questions: what would enough actually look like for you? like specifically
whose definition of success are you still measuring yourself against?

rows.title: the teacher's teacher
rows.body: faith that survived doubt can hold other people's doubt too. the questioners find you, because you're the one who questioned everything and still stands somewhere. saturn appointed you to that post, and you keep showing up to it.
self_questions: which questioner found you, and what did you hold for them?

rows.title: authority sits loose
rows.body: when leadership lands on you, and it does, you wear it like a borrowed coat. you run the thing well and hand it back without a flicker of grief.
self_questions: what did you lead well and release easily?

rows.title: you process by moving
rows.body: your feelings live in your body and they exit through it too. bad day means a walk, a run, cleaning the whole kitchen at midnight. sitting still with a feeling makes it worse. motion is how you digest.
self_questions: where do you go when something's eating you?

rows.title: friends became audience
rows.body: somewhere along the way the circle turned into a crowd, and crowds can't hold your hand. the people who knew you before the reach remember a version you've been too busy to visit.
self_questions: who knew you before the audience did?

rows.title: whose finish line is it
rows.body: sometimes the finish line you're running toward was drawn by someone else. family. an old version of you. worth checking whose handwriting is on it before you spend another year running.
self_questions: whose definition of success are you still measuring yourself against?

rows.title: compassion charges you
rows.body: mercy given, beauty made, the moment spirit gets into the room. giving from the boundless refills you, which never made sense on paper and has never once failed in practice.
self_questions: what giving filled you back up?

rows.title: it leaks as the unmade masterpiece
rows.body: the novel, the album, the business. circling for years, always almost started. making it would risk finding out it's ordinary, so it stays perfect and imaginary instead.
self_questions: what have you protected by never making it?

rows.title: the keeper of the hearth
rows.body: in your family or your circle, the feelings gather at your place. you hold the traditions, the gatherings, the emotional archive of the group. somebody has to, and it was always going to be you.
self_questions: what do you keep for everyone?

rows.title: belonging arrives late
rows.body: your people came late. the tribe that actually fits found you well into the story, and the fit was worth every strange, unmatched year that came before it.
self_questions: what were the unmatched years for, looking back?

rows.title: the thin ice memory
rows.body: errors always felt expensive to you, like the ice was thin and one wrong step genuinely mattered. so you check. and check. the ice got thicker years ago. the checking hasn't heard.
self_questions: what are you still double checking that stopped being thin ice?

rows.title: you grieve in secret
rows.body: your losses get processed alone, sometimes so privately that people never knew there was a loss. it protects you. it also means nobody knows to bring the casserole.
self_questions: what loss did you carry without telling anyone?

rows.title: enough is a superpower
rows.body: your immunity to more is rare wealth. it means your choices get made on truer axes than acquisition. guard it. the world sells hard, and you're one of the few it can't reach.
self_questions: what has being unbuyable let you choose?

rows.title: growth that compounds
rows.body: your expansion is quiet and cumulative. the skill built over years, the savings, the garden, the name that means something. nothing about your growth is dramatic and all of it is permanent. you get rich slow, in every currency.
self_questions: what have you been quietly compounding?

rows.title: the mind from orbit
rows.body: you see systems where others see situations. patterns, structures, the rules underneath the rules. it makes your take on any problem arrive from an angle nobody had a chair facing.
self_questions: what do you see in the system that the people inside it can't?

rows.title: anger from the front
rows.body: your fury is grand but never sneaky. you announce the grievance from the podium, in full view, and the openness is its own kind of honesty. nobody's ever been ambushed by you.
self_questions: when did announcing your anger openly change the fight?

rows.title: scorched earth clarity
rows.body: sometimes the only way you can see a situation clearly is after you've burned it down. quitting, ending, deleting everything. destruction is your reading light.
self_questions: what did you have to end before you could understand it?

rows.title: the serious side gets no airtime
rows.body: you've been funny so long that when you're actually serious, people wait for the punchline. it's lonely in a way that's hard to explain. even your heaviest stuff gets a laugh track.
self_questions: what do you wish someone would take seriously the first time?

rows.title: it leaks as interruption
rows.body: you finish people's thoughts, jump the gaps, reach for the mic. waiting while someone else talks costs you visible effort, and everyone can see the meter running.
self_questions: whose sentences do you keep finishing?

rows.title: small perfect things
rows.body: you'd rather make one small thing exactly right than ten things approximately. the world rewards volume. you keep voting for precision anyway.
self_questions: what's the smallest thing you've ever been proudest of?

rows.title: the quick face
rows.body: you read as light on arrival. curious, funny, always a question loaded. people leave a first meeting with you feeling interesting, and they never notice you steered the whole thing. what they got was maybe ten percent of what was actually running in your head.
self_questions: what did the last new person you met walk away knowing about you?

rows.title: you're built for the crossing
rows.body: fed right, this hunger makes you the one who walks others through their worst. you've been to the underworld enough times to give tours. that's a job, and almost nobody can do it.
self_questions: who could you walk through the dark right now?

rows.title: all or nothing
rows.body: you don't do casual feelings. when you love it's total, when you're hurt it goes to the bone, and when you're done it's forever. the middle settings never worked on you. people get let all the way in or kept all the way out.
self_questions: who got all the way in?

rows.title: the vault
rows.body: people tell you things they've never told anyone. you keep every secret like it's your own, which is the problem, because now they live in you too.
self_questions: which secret has been living in you the longest?

rows.title: the almost there ache
rows.body: your life is a series of thresholds. one more level, one more year, then it'll be real. arrival keeps moving. the ache of almost is your home address.
self_questions: what would actually count as arriving?

rows.title: the beautiful hunger
rows.body: you're soothed by beautiful things the way other people are soothed by advice. good light, good fabric, food that took hours. it's not shallow, it's your nervous system's language. when life gets loud, you don't want a talk. you want a clean room, a warm meal, and something lovely to look at.
self_questions: what's the first beautiful thing you remember wanting?
what does your version of enough look like?

rows.title: never the first answer
rows.body: the official version, the press release, the surface explanation, your mind treats all of it as chapter one. there's always more underneath, and assuming so has been right too many times to stop.
self_questions: what official story have you never bought?

rows.title: the mother thread
rows.body: your emotional baseline was set early, in the house you grew up in, by whoever mothered you, however that went. the echo is still audible in how you soothe yourself now.
self_questions: what did comfort look like in your first home?

rows.title: useful mastery feeds you
rows.body: being skilled and needed in the same moment is your generator. the craft applied to a real problem for a real person, that's the current your whole system runs on.
self_questions: when were you last skilled and needed at once?

rows.title: the champion setting
rows.body: you fight best as somebody's champion. give you a person to defend, a cause to carry into the arena, and the performance becomes real power. representing is your fire's highest gear.
self_questions: who are you champion for?

rows.title: pleasure is a practice
rows.body: you actually enjoy things, in the present tense, with full attention. most people lost that skill somewhere and don't know it's missing. yours never left, and it makes your ordinary days richer than their special ones.
self_questions: what did you fully enjoy this week, with nothing else running?

rows.title: the weight nobody sees
rows.body: you do your hardest work in private. the doubts, the fears, the figuring-yourself-out. nobody really knows how much you carry because you don't show it. it's not hiding exactly. it's just where your work gets done.
self_questions: what's the hardest thing you've done that nobody clapped for?

rows.title: loving the idea of them
rows.body: you've fallen for concepts of people. the fascinating version, the theoretical them, curated by your own interest. the actual human underneath got missed a few times, and one of them noticed.
self_questions: who did you love in theory more than in person?

rows.title: both sides of your own heart
rows.body: you can argue both sides of your own feelings so well that deciding what you actually want takes forever. the weighing is honest, and it's also a great place to hide from choosing.
self_questions: what decision have you been weighing too long?

rows.title: the guarded harvest
rows.body: saturn sits on your softness. feeling safe, belonging, letting people all the way in, none of it came standard. somewhere early the walls went up for good reasons, and everything tender in your life since was grown behind them, on purpose, by hand.
self_questions: what tenderness did you grow behind the walls?

rows.title: the keeper
rows.body: you're the one entrusted with continuity. the recipes, the standards, the stories, the things that must not be lost. groups hand you their permanence without a ceremony, and you keep it without a complaint.
self_questions: what have you been entrusted to keep?

rows.title: the draft is never done
rows.body: you reread sent messages. you revise texts nobody will see again. every piece of your own writing is one pass from acceptable, permanently. shipping anything requires physically stopping yourself.
self_questions: what did you send and immediately want back for one more edit?

rows.title: anger goes quiet
rows.body: hurt you and the temperature drops. the silence is the fight, and everyone in your house can read the barometer by now. you've won arguments without saying a word for three days.
self_questions: who can read your silence fluently?

rows.title: first responder courage
rows.body: in real danger you move while others freeze. your body volunteers before the vote. it's the fire's best setting, and everyone who's been in a crisis with you knows it.
self_questions: when did your body move before your mind caught up?

rows.title: courage arrives with age
rows.body: every year you get braver. the assertiveness that terrified you at twenty runs routine at forty. your fire matures on a schedule, like it's been on saturn's payroll the whole time.
self_questions: what's easy now that once took everything?

rows.title: you make hard things simple
rows.body: you can take something complicated and hand it to someone in words they actually get. people leave conversations with you understanding their own thoughts better. that's a skill, and you've had it so long you forget it's rare.
self_questions: what do people always ask you to explain?

rows.title: creating charges you
rows.body: making things, performing things, producing delight from nothing. creation is your generator, and your most tired weeks are always, on inspection, your least creative ones.
self_questions: what have you made lately, and did you notice it recharged you?

rows.title: the slow sure mind
rows.body: your thinking moves like a truck with a full load. slow to start, hard to stop, and it arrives with everything intact. you don't do hot takes. by the time you say a thing, you've tested it, and it holds.
self_questions: what opinion of yours has never needed updating?

rows.title: gather them toward something
rows.body: fed right, this hunger builds true communities and lifts whole groups. you're wired to gather people, and that's rare. point the gathering at something real, and the numbers finally mean what you always wanted them to.
self_questions: what could your crowd become if it had a direction?

rows.title: worry is how you love
rows.body: when you love someone, you start working. planning, fixing, remembering their appointments, noticing what they need before they do. worry is your heart's way of paying attention. if you've stopped fussing over someone, that's the real goodbye.
self_questions: who do you worry about the most?

rows.title: allergic to waiting
rows.body: waiting rooms, loading screens, people who take forever to get to the point. your whole body registers slowness as pain. you'd rather do it twice fast than once slow.
self_questions: what's the longest you've ever let something take its time?

rows.title: the torchbearer
rows.body: your role is carrying fire back to people who lost theirs. conversations with you relight people's why, and half of them never mention it. the torch gets passed in sentences you don't remember saying.
self_questions: whose why did you relight?

rows.title: old before your time
rows.body: you were the responsible one early, maybe too early. somewhere back there a kid learned that feelings wait until the work is done. the good news is the steadiness is real. the other news is the kid is still waiting.
self_questions: when did you first become the responsible one?

rows.title: earned faith
rows.body: you can't just believe things. you have to test them, doubt them, rebuild them brick by brick. it's slower than everyone else's faith. it's also why yours holds.
self_questions: what do you believe now that you had to earn the hard way?

rows.title: the schooled fire
rows.body: saturn sits on your will. starting things, asserting yourself, saying i want out loud, all of it came with a resistance most people never feel. you learned to act anyway. every ounce of your courage is earned, not issued, and it shows in how you carry it.
self_questions: what did asserting yourself used to cost you?

rows.title: the standard
rows.body: you hold yourself to a bar nobody set for you out loud. showing up underdressed, underprepared, or underdelivered physically pains you, even for things that don't matter.
self_questions: who would actually be disappointed, if you're honest?

rows.title: alone time is food
rows.body: you need time alone the way other people need company. it's not antisocial. it's how you refill. the only trick is knowing the difference between resting alone and hiding alone.
self_questions: when did being alone last feel good instead of lonely?

rows.title: the fortress becomes a home
rows.body: the walls you built young make an unbreakable shelter now, for you and everyone you let inside. protection was the first draft. sanctuary is the final one, and you're living in it.
self_questions: who shelters inside what you built?

rows.title: the fog retreat
rows.body: mid-conflict, you sometimes just leave. still present, fully absent, unfindable. fights can't finish against a ghost, and some of yours have been technically open for years.
self_questions: which fight did you exit without ending?

rows.title: lit means leading yourself
rows.body: at full vitality, your life is something you initiate daily, not something that happens to you. the question that keeps you bright is simple and it renews every morning. what will you start today.
self_questions: what will you start today?

rows.title: lit means held too
rows.body: at full vitality, the shelter runs both ways. you're inside somebody's care as well as providing your own, and the harbor finally has a harbor. don't skip that half. it's where your brightest years are.
self_questions: who holds the harbor keeper?

rows.title: built to last
rows.body: your taste runs classic. the enduring over the trending, the proven over the shiny, the coat that works for twenty years. you love few things and love them for decades, and everything you've chosen has outlived its fashion.
self_questions: what have you loved for over a decade?

rows.title: the quotation memory
rows.body: you remember what people said, verbatim, years later. the compliment, the cruelty, the promise. words are permanent objects to you, and you're often startled that others just drop theirs anywhere.
self_questions: which sentence has lived in you the longest?

rows.title: you feel for the group
rows.body: what happens to your people happens to you. the team's loss, the community's fight, the friend group's rupture, all of it runs through your own chest like it's personal. because to you it is.
self_questions: whose cause sits in your chest?

rows.title: louder isn't landing
rows.body: volume went up, reach went up, and the heard feeling stayed missing. more decibels keep not being the same thing as more understood, and the gap is where the hunger lives.
self_questions: when did being loud last actually work?

rows.title: shower crier
rows.body: you cry in the shower, in the car, in the dark of a movie. it's not a breakdown, it's maintenance. afterwards you feel oddly new, like a city after rain.
self_questions: when did you last let the rain actually finish?

rows.title: here to make it work
rows.body: you're here to make things actually function, for actual people. the healed body, the fixed system, the process that stopped failing the ones inside it. your life force is useful mastery, and everything downstream of your hands runs better than it would have.
self_questions: what works because you made it work?

rows.title: the late bloom into view
rows.body: your visibility came years after your talent. the room found you late, and you were more than ready, because the waiting years were building years, every one of them.
self_questions: what were you ready for long before anyone looked?

rows.title: metaphor is your first language
rows.body: you explain everything by way of something else. it's like when, imagine if, think of it as. direct description feels like drawing with a ruler. the sideways route is where your precision actually lives.
self_questions: what's your favorite explanation you've ever built from an it's like?

rows.title: movements leave you unmoved
rows.body: causes and communities recruit you constantly and never quite land. group belonging is a language you understand perfectly and simply don't speak.
self_questions: what group tried hardest to claim you?

rows.title: friendship is the doorway
rows.body: every real love of yours started as fascination between friends. romance without the friendship underneath has never once worked on you, and never will. the crush is optional. the conversation isn't.
self_questions: which love started as your favorite conversation?

rows.title: nothing left to fear losing
rows.body: having settled your account with endings, you can risk what others can't. the fearlessness is quiet and completely real. spend it on the things that actually matter, because almost nobody else has it to spend.
self_questions: what could you risk that others couldn't survive risking?

rows.title: justice starts the engine
rows.body: you struggle to fight for your own preference and ignite instantly at unfairness. give the fight a principle and your whole reluctance evaporates. the cause is the key.
self_questions: what injustice reliably lights you?

rows.title: pursuit as courtship
rows.body: everything you chase gets courted. the job gets wooed, the goal gets dazzled, the dream gets flowers. your drive doesn't grind toward things, it romances them.
self_questions: what are you currently courting?

rows.title: elsewhere always looks prettier
rows.body: your taste for the foreign has discounted the near. some of your best things went unappreciated until you left them, and the leaving was the only lens that ever showed you what they were.
self_questions: what did you only see clearly after leaving it?

rows.title: the diplomat
