rows.body: you can talk to anyone. the difficult relative, the angry client, both sides of the feud. you bend the conversation like wind bends grass, and everyone leaves thinking you agreed with them.
self_questions: where did you learn to read a room like a weather map?

rows.title: the two-faced fire
rows.body: you run hotter than you show. under the functional daytime self there's an intensity, convictions, obsessions, a capacity for extremes, that only a few people have ever seen at full flame. you transform through burning: every few years a version of you goes into the fire and someone renovated walks out. people who knew the old versions compare notes and can't agree on who you are. all of them are right.
self_questions: which version of you went into the last fire?
who has seen the full flame?

rows.title: read as aloof about yourself
rows.body: your lack of self-promotion gets mistaken for low confidence, or mystery, or both. the subject of you just doesn't hold you. there are more interesting rooms in the house.
self_questions: who misreads your quiet about yourself?

rows.title: lit means channeled
rows.body: at full vitality, the boundless in you has a form to arrive through. the art, the service, the healing work. when it flows through you into the world instead of pooling, you're the brightest thing in any room, and the room can tell.
self_questions: what form is the boundless asking for right now?

rows.title: unsinkable
rows.body: criticism rolls off you at a rate people find suspicious. it's not that you don't hear it. it's that your buoyancy was decided long ago, privately, and the vote isn't reopening.
self_questions: whose opinion actually gets through?

rows.title: the slow burn
rows.body: your drive is torque, not speed. slow to anger, slow to start, unstoppable once moving. people mistake the quiet for softness right up until they're pushing against you and nothing is moving.
self_questions: what did someone learn by pushing you?

rows.title: homesick everywhere
rows.body: you're hungry for a home you can't name. every place is almost it. you rearrange, relocate, renovate, and the settled feeling visits but won't move in. the address you're looking for might not be a place.
self_questions: what would finally feel like home?

rows.title: the fidget
rows.body: your hands are never still. pen spinning, label peeling, dough that didn't strictly need kneading. stillness lives in your fingers or it doesn't live at all.
self_questions: what are your hands doing when you're anxious versus when you're happy?

rows.title: rivals get invented
rows.body: no enemy around, and you'll quietly promote a coworker to one without telling them. the competition is sometimes real and sometimes cast, and you're the casting director either way.
self_questions: who's your current rival, and do they know?

rows.title: loved by your whole gravity
rows.body: being chosen by you is unforgettable. nobody you've ever loved felt generic while it lasted, and most of them measure everything after against it. that gravity is rare. aim it like you know it.
self_questions: who still measures things against your love?

rows.title: the one who stays
rows.body: you're the ally. the person who shows up on moving day, co-signs the plan, stands in the wedding and the waiting room both. your love is not fireworks, it's infrastructure, and people build their lives on it, sometimes without noticing they have. being taken for granted is the tax on being dependable, and you pay it quietly.
self_questions: who shows up for you the way you show up for them?
what promise are you still keeping that nobody remembers you made?

rows.title: drawn to the wounded
rows.body: the broken-winged keep finding you, and you keep opening the door. rescuing and romancing have blurred, expensively, more than once. some of your loves were really shifts at a clinic that never paid.
self_questions: which love was actually a rescue in costume?

rows.title: the control clause
rows.body: your excess is grip. the need to hold the outcome, the mystery, the other person's process. some of your growth is standing just past the edge of your grip, waiting for you to open the hand.
self_questions: what would grow if you let go of it?

rows.title: the future's soldier
rows.body: your fights age well. the weird hill you defended becomes next decade's consensus, over and over. being early to the right side of things is your fire's track record.
self_questions: what hill are you early on right now?

rows.title: the throne you didn't ask for
rows.body: you carry your people with you. the ones before you, the name, the standard someone set generations back. even when nobody's watching you act like somebody is, because in your bones somebody always is. it gives you a dignity people notice within minutes of meeting you. it also means you rarely feel fully off duty.
self_questions: whose approval are you still performing for?
what part of the inheritance do you actually want?

rows.title: half of you is always negotiating
rows.body: you track the relationship's temperature constantly. reading, adjusting, managing the us like a second job with no days off. somewhere in the managing, the being-in-it got outsourced.
self_questions: when did you last just be in it, instead of running it?

rows.title: the closed door hours
rows.body: you need sealed-off time like other people need meals. hours alone, unaccounted for, recharging in ways you never explain. anyone who takes it personally doesn't get to stay.
self_questions: what actually happens in your sealed hours?

rows.title: you wait for backup
rows.body: you fight best with an ally beside you and hesitate alone. some battles waited years for a second that never came, battles you could have won solo on day one.
self_questions: what fight are you postponing until someone stands with you?

rows.title: words with weight
rows.body: because you say less, yours count double. rooms quiet slightly when you finally speak, and you've noticed. that's the interest saturn pays on a decade of careful deposits.
self_questions: where does your word carry the most weight now?

rows.title: generous like a king
rows.body: when you give, you give formally, fully, a little grandly. splitting a bill bores you. covering the whole table feels right. it's not showing off, it's how care is supposed to look where you come from.
self_questions: what did generosity look like in your house growing up?

rows.title: the word weird follows you
rows.body: you've been called weird since before you knew it was a category. you were just saying what you actually thought. eventually you stopped translating and let the label do its thing. the right people find you by it.
self_questions: when did you stop translating yourself?

rows.title: big game only
rows.body: your pursuits are horizon-sized. small targets can't hold your draw, and you've let a hundred minor wins walk past while you tracked something worth the arrow.
self_questions: what's the big game you're tracking now?

rows.title: the locked gaze
rows.body: when you want something, the wanting organizes your entire life. you'll wait years, work in the dark, endure being unchosen and unnoticed, because your eye is on a prize most people can't even see yet. it's the forked branch: two paths, and you burning to have both. the people who love you learn that your intensity isn't against them. it's just that you're always mid-hunt.
self_questions: what's the prize your whole life is quietly arranged around?
what have you sacrificed to the goal without deciding to?

rows.title: soft is the hard part
rows.body: being comforted embarrasses you a little. when you're hurt, your instinct is to get angry or get busy, anything but be held. the people who love you have learned to sneak the care in sideways.
self_questions: who's allowed to see you hurt?

rows.title: growth after the dues
rows.body: your expansions come late and large. years of quiet dues, then a door that opens all at once and stays open. the pattern has repeated enough to trust. the wait was never wasted, it was the price printing.
self_questions: what dues are you paying right now, and for which door?

rows.title: here to move the future closer
rows.body: you're here on behalf of what's next. seeing what could be and pulling it toward now, one strange idea at a time. your life force runs on vision, and things exist today because you insisted on them before they were reasonable.
self_questions: what did you insist on before it was reasonable?

rows.title: pain has to mean something
rows.body: you can carry almost anything if it has a point. the lesson, the growth, the story it becomes. meaningless suffering is the only kind that actually breaks you, so your heart works overtime turning wounds into wisdom.
self_questions: what hard thing are you still looking for the meaning in?

rows.title: you rebuild in the dark
rows.body: your biggest emotional changes happen privately and completely. people see you fine, then see you changed, and never see the middle. the construction site was always closed to visitors.
self_questions: what did you go through that nobody watched?

rows.title: anger arrives late
rows.body: in the moment you're calm. tuesday you're furious about saturday, once the full weight of it lands. your anger runs on a delay, and it's always about something that deserved it.
self_questions: what are you just now getting angry about?

rows.title: luck respects your record
rows.body: your opportunities come from reputation. the recommendation, the call that came because they knew your work. you're lucky in the boring way, which is the way that keeps working.
self_questions: what door did your track record open without you knocking?

rows.title: looking foolish burns
rows.body: you can take pain in private like a champ. but stumbling in front of people, getting it wrong where everyone can see. that burns different and lasts longer. some risks you've skipped just to avoid the audience.
self_questions: what would you try if nobody could watch?

rows.title: small talk turns to fog
rows.body: the light chatter everyone runs on drifts past you. mid-conversation you sometimes notice you left several minutes ago, and nobody caught it.
self_questions: where do you go when the chatter starts?

rows.title: the deep water
rows.body: your stillness is not emptiness, it's depth. you contain things, your own storms, other people's chaos, years of feeling, without surface disturbance, like the far bottom of the sea where the weather doesn't reach. people bring you their panic because your calm is contagious and your discretion is total. it took real pain to get this deep. that's the part the calm never mentions.
self_questions: what storms are you containing right now?
what pain built your depth?

rows.title: last on your own list
rows.body: you notice everyone's needs with surgical precision and treat your own like spam. rest, help, comfort, all flagged as things for later. the standard you keep for caring stops applying the moment it points at you.
self_questions: what do you need that you keep postponing?

rows.title: quiet resentment ledger
rows.body: you'd never invoice anyone for your loyalty, but somewhere in you there's a ledger, and some entries are old. it only surfaces when you're exhausted, and it surprises everyone including you.
self_questions: what entry in the ledger needs to be forgiven or said?

rows.title: the before and after
rows.body: your life doesn't change gradually. it changes in chapters. big before-and-after moments that split time in two. and every time, you come back changed and somehow more yourself.
self_questions: what moment split your life into a before and an after?

rows.title: the room's thermostat
rows.body: you feel a conversation tilting toward tension and adjust before anyone notices. a joke here, a subject change there. people think the vibe was just naturally good. the vibe was labor.
self_questions: what does it cost you to keep everything smooth?

rows.title: generous with the ladder
rows.body: you remember exactly how hard the climb was, so you lower the ladder constantly. advice, intros, cover, second chances. your protégés multiply. your own mentors were mostly imaginary.
self_questions: who lowered a ladder for you, even once?

rows.title: a win repairs the mood
rows.body: achievement genuinely soothes you. finishing the thing, the recognition, the shipped project. it's real regulation, and it runs on a refill schedule that never quite lets you rest.
self_questions: what win are you chasing to feel better?

rows.title: the heart needs a horizon
rows.body: freedom keeps you emotionally alive. a trip planned, a future imagined, a door left open. the moment something feels like a cage, even a comfortable one, your mood drops through the floor. you love people best when nobody's holding the leash.
self_questions: what's the open door you need to know is there?

rows.title: the igniter
rows.body: in every group you've ever been in, you're the one who makes it actually start. meetings become projects when you enter. ideas become schedules. somebody has to strike the match, and it was always going to be you.
self_questions: what did you ignite that's still burning?

rows.title: growth by refinement
rows.body: you expand by getting better, not bigger. the craft sharpened, the process improved, the skill taken from good to undeniable. while others scale, you perfect. and perfection, it turns out, scales.
self_questions: what have you refined into your fortune?

rows.title: discord dims you
rows.body: prolonged conflict environments drain you below the waterline. the fighting household, the warring team. others adapt to it. your system pays for every day of it, and the bill shows.
self_questions: what discord is currently billing you?

rows.title: conformity dims you
rows.body: long stretches of pretending to be standard drain you at the root. the normal costume fits, technically, and every day inside it costs light. you were never the problem the fitting-in was solving.
self_questions: where are you still wearing the costume?

rows.title: lit means mid-pilgrimage
rows.body: at full vitality, your life is a pilgrimage you're always in the middle of, sharing the road as you walk it. arrival was never the point of you. the lit state is both feet on the path, telling the story live.
self_questions: where is the path pointing now?

rows.title: you teach people to take up space
rows.body: your example gives quieter people permission. someone became braver about being visible because they watched you refuse to shrink. your bigness is a license other people use.
self_questions: who takes up more space because you showed them how?

rows.title: the early exit
rows.body: you leave good parties at their peak. not because you're unhappy, but because some part of you wonders what else the night is hiding.
self_questions: what are you hoping is out there past the good moment?

rows.title: the deep discipline
rows.body: saturn sits in your depths. control, trust, letting anything hold power over you, all of it schooled hard and early. you learned to survive on your own authority alone. the lesson still running is that surrender, chosen carefully, is its own kind of strength.
self_questions: what is saturn still teaching you about letting go?

rows.title: drawn to grace
rows.body: you're attracted to elegance of motion. manners, timing, the way someone moves through a room without disturbing its balance. gracelessness has undone more attractions for you than any flaw of face.
self_questions: whose grace caught you before their words did?

rows.title: the soft morning
rows.body: your ideal day starts slow. anyone who schedules you before ten learns something about your true nature. the world was designed by morning people and you've decided to forgive it.
self_questions: what does your perfect slow morning actually contain?

rows.title: drawn to the one-of-one
rows.body: you're attracted to the self-invented. the person who built their own taste, their own path, their own weird. copies do nothing for you, however polished. originality is the whole aphrodisiac.
self_questions: who's the most original person you ever fell for?

rows.title: guru after guru
rows.body: the podcast sage, the book that changed everything, the practice that was it. six months each, roughly. the shelf of former answers is long, and it's still somehow a shrine.
self_questions: who was the last teacher that was supposed to be final?

rows.title: the royal fight
rows.body: your drive is proud and public. you fight with honor rules, no cheap shots, no ganging up, dignity available for both sides. you want to win, but you want to win well, in the open, with witnesses.
self_questions: what rules do you fight by that your opponents don't?

rows.title: completion instinct
rows.body: you finish things gently, the goodbye done right, the project landed softly, the last day honored. others rush endings out of discomfort. you understand that the ending is part of the thing.
self_questions: what deserves a proper ending that hasn't gotten one?

rows.title: dreams do the processing
rows.body: your sleep works a night shift. the day's unfinished feelings show up in dreams, and you wake with answers you didn't fall asleep holding. the back office never closes.
self_questions: what has a dream told you lately?

rows.title: pretty has fooled you
rows.body: the beautiful package has sold you empty boxes. charm outvoted character at least twice, and by the time the contents settled, you'd already fallen for the wrapping. your eye is a gift with a known exploit.
self_questions: when did the wrapping win against the contents?

rows.title: boundary weather
rows.body: your no has always been softer than your yes. people lean on you past reason and you let them, then wonder why you're depleted. the flock is fed. the shepherd forgot to eat.
self_questions: where does your softness need a fence?

rows.title: the slow steady heart
rows.body: your heart runs on steadiness. you don't fall fast, you don't leave fast, and once someone's in, they're in for years. what you want from love is simple and rare. stay, be consistent, don't make me guess.
self_questions: who has actually stayed?

rows.title: affection as adventure
rows.body: love, for you, is doing things together. the mission, the trip, the 2am idea acted on immediately. sitting quietly side by side is fine for other people. your romance needs a pulse.
self_questions: what's the best thing you ever did with someone you loved?

rows.title: the feelings live offstage
rows.body: your real emotional life happens where nobody's watching. alone, at night, in the car, in the shower. what people see day to day is the summary. the full text stays private.
self_questions: where does your real feeling happen?

rows.title: you give from an empty tank
rows.body: your generosity doesn't check the fuel gauge. you'll pour into your people while running on fumes and call it fine. the ones who love you back have learned to watch the gauge for you.
self_questions: who checks on the giver?

rows.title: the bookkeeper stays
rows.body: the lean years left a bookkeeper in you. even in good seasons, part of you is still packing for winter, still counting, still checking the pantry of your whole life twice.
self_questions: what winter are you still packing for?

rows.title: weird sources, real insight
rows.body: your best ideas come from corners no syllabus includes. the niche forum, the dead philosopher, the manual for something unrelated. you cross-pollinate on purpose, and it's why your thinking can't be predicted from your inputs.
self_questions: what's the strangest source that ever taught you something real?

rows.title: surface and depth
rows.body: people assume the polish means shallow. they learn. the shine is load-bearing, and underneath it there's an engineer who earned every glint.
self_questions: who has underestimated you most usefully?

rows.title: tidal strength
rows.body: your power comes in waves and runs deepest in defense. as a protector you're genuinely fearsome. the perimeter you hold around your people has never once been breached on your watch.
self_questions: whose perimeter are you holding?

rows.title: growth needs a fight
rows.body: you expand under challenge and shrink in comfort. the easy seasons made you restless, the hard ones made you more. an opponent, a deadline, a mountain, something to push against is your actual fertilizer.
self_questions: what are you pushing against right now?

rows.title: it leaks as the borrowed life
rows.body: fiction, other people's stories, lives you watch instead of live. whole evenings spent in worlds with no address. the watching is rich and real. it's also, some nights, instead.
self_questions: what are you watching instead of living lately?

rows.title: the mind that edits
rows.body: everything that enters your head gets improved on the way through. the plan gets a revision, the sentence gets tightened, the idea gets stress tested. thinking and fixing are the same motion for you.
self_questions: what did you mentally rewrite today?

rows.title: drawn to the depths
rows.body: you're attracted to mystery. the scar with a story, the locked room in a person, the thing they don't say at parties. transparent people are pleasant, and opaque people are magnetic, and you've never once confused the two.
self_questions: whose locked room drew you in?

rows.title: small talk is the front door
rows.body: people who hate small talk think it's the whole house. for you it's just the door. give you three minutes on the weather and you'll know who someone is. the light stuff is how you take the temperature.
self_questions: what's the best thing you ever learned from a throwaway conversation?

rows.title: midnight starts
rows.body: your best beginnings happen at strange hours. new plans, new workouts, new lives, all drafted after midnight with total certainty. mornings are for other people's doubts.
self_questions: what did you start this month, and where is it now?

rows.title: build the inner address
rows.body: fed right, this hunger makes sanctuary builders. the home you're starving for gets built inside first, and then every place you live inherits it. you've had the deed the whole time.
self_questions: what would an inner home be made of?

rows.title: no hedge words
rows.body: perhaps, arguably, it could be said. these words don't survive in your sentences. you commit to the take fully, and if you're wrong, you'll be wrong at full volume and correct it with equal confidence.
self_questions: what were you magnificently wrong about?

rows.title: your face leaks the weather
rows.body: you say you're fine and your face files a different report. everyone close to you knows the tells. the quiet, the slightly off smile. you've never once hidden a mood from someone paying attention.
self_questions: who reads your weather before you announce it?

rows.title: you teach patience
rows.body: people around you learn to wait well by watching. your pace gives others permission to stop sprinting. more than one person has slowed down into a better life because your speed looked so livable.
self_questions: who learned to slow down from you?

rows.title: the wit test
rows.body: attraction switches on at the first good joke and starts dying at the first dull hour. gorgeous and boring has never once beaten plain and funny in your entire history, and it never will.
self_questions: who passed the wit test instantly?

rows.title: fed feelings
rows.body: comfort and food are wired together in you. a good meal repairs a bad day, and the fridge gets opened when the heart does. some of your best emotional care has been served on a plate.
self_questions: what's your repair meal?

rows.title: the storm system
rows.body: your feelings arrive like weather. sudden, total, and then completely gone, leaving everything washed and strangely clear. people who fear storms find you too much. people who've lived through a few know your rain is how things get clean.
self_questions: what does your after-the-storm clarity usually tell you?
who has stayed through your worst weather?

rows.title: second chances
rows.body: you give them. maybe too many. people write themselves off and you're still holding the door, because you know what it's like to come back from something.
self_questions: who got a chance from you that they didn't use?

rows.title: the family historian
rows.body: you remember. birthdays, grudges, the story of how your people got here. others forget and drift. you hold the record, sometimes resentfully, always thoroughly.
self_questions: which family story explains you best?

rows.title: signal in the noise
rows.body: in any argument or crisis, you hear the actual issue under the shouting. you can't always fix it, but you can name it, and naming it is often the whole fix.
self_questions: what's the real issue under the current noise in your life?

rows.title: the search that doesn't end
rows.body: you're always slightly looking for something. a better word, a better city, a feeling you can't describe but would recognize instantly. it makes you a wonderful finder of things and a restless keeper of them. the search isn't a phase. it's the engine.
self_questions: what are you actually looking for, in one honest sentence?
what have you found that you let yourself keep?

rows.title: the soulmate lens
rows.body: every love feels fated. cosmic, written, meant. ordinary matches feel like blasphemy against something, and you'd rather be alone than settle for a love with no mythology.
self_questions: which love felt written before it started?

rows.title: slow to anger, biblical when there
rows.body: your fuse is measured in years. people mistake it for infinite. it isn't, and the two or three eruptions of your life are still discussed by witnesses in hushed tones.
self_questions: what finally reaches the bottom of your patience?

rows.title: the tide fights
rows.body: your drive dissolves and returns. direct combat fails you, and then you win by yielding, absorbing, outlasting, flowing around. anger confuses itself in your body on the way out. your strength never looked like anyone else's, and it was never once fake.
self_questions: what did you win by yielding?

rows.title: the emergency brain
rows.body: in any crisis you're already three steps in. who to call, what to freeze, where the documents are. people marvel at your calm. it's not calm, it's rehearsal. part of you is always braced.
self_questions: when did you first have to be the adult in the room?

rows.title: drawn to the radiant
rows.body: you're attracted to shine. talent mid-performance, confidence mid-stride, anyone lit up by what they love. glow finds glow, and you've never once fallen for someone at their dimmest.
self_questions: who was glowing when you fell for them?

rows.title: love in gold leaf
rows.body: your taste runs warm and generous. the beautiful gesture, the occasion made special, the full production of delight. minimalism is a fine philosophy for people who don't know what a celebration is for.
self_questions: what's the most beautiful gesture you ever made?

rows.title: the long campaign
rows.body: your drive is patience with teeth. you fight in campaigns, not battles. planned, provisioned, timed to the season. your anger is cold, controlled, and converted directly into work. you don't get mad. you get organized.
self_questions: what campaign are you running that looks like ordinary work?

rows.title: the fuse costs you
rows.body: the speed that wins you battles loses you moments. words launched before the check cleared. some repairs took years longer than the ten seconds that caused them.
self_questions: which ten seconds are you still repairing?

rows.title: loyal past the exit
rows.body: you stay loyal to people who've left. old friends, old bosses, exes even, you defend them in rooms they'll never know about. leaving your heart is a much slower process than leaving your life.
self_questions: who are you still loyal to that you no longer speak to?

rows.title: it leaks as self-audit
rows.body: everyone else seems able to just relax into who they are. you keep reviewing yourself, adjusting, checking the fit of your own personality. comfortable in your own skin is a rumor you're still investigating.
self_questions: when do you stop auditing yourself?

rows.title: quiet pride
rows.body: there's a pride in you that almost nobody knows about. you don't perform it. but being underestimated? that one stings more than you let on.
self_questions: when did being underestimated last sting?

rows.title: growth through curiosity
rows.body: you expand by asking. every question opens two more doors, every conversation is a possible hallway. your life keeps getting bigger, and never through plans. through wait, tell me more.
self_questions: what question changed your direction?

rows.title: two moods at once
rows.body: you can be heartbroken and laughing in the same hour and mean both. people find it confusing. for you it's just tuesday. feelings don't take turns in there, they overlap.
self_questions: what two things are you feeling at once right now?

rows.title: own money, own keys
rows.body: splitting everything, keeping your own account, your own exit route. it's not distrust exactly. it's that depending on someone fully feels like forgetting how to swim.
self_questions: what's the difference for you between depending and drowning?

rows.title: the fear of the closed door
rows.body: belonging never felt guaranteed to you. part of you still checks whether you're really invited, really wanted, really in. old doors left that, and the checking never fully retired.
self_questions: where do you still check if you're really wanted?

rows.title: loving the potential
rows.body: sometimes you fall for who someone could be. the draft version. and then you quietly start on the edits. real rest is the people you don't need to improve.
self_questions: who can you be around without fixing anything?

rows.title: the small things are the love
rows.body: grand gestures make you suspicious. your love lives in refilled prescriptions, charged phones, the thing they mentioned once in march showing up in july. anyone can do a big moment. you do the maintenance.
self_questions: what tiny thing do you do that nobody clocks as love?

rows.title: the calm you walk in with
rows.body: you slow a room down just by being in it. people meet you and assume nothing rattles you, that you've got somewhere comfortable to be and no rush getting there. steady reads as safe, so people trust you with real things early. and mostly they're right to.
self_questions: what do people hand you because you look like you can hold it?

rows.title: the too-big check
rows.body: your excess is grandeur. the plan with no budget, the gesture that outran the wallet, the promise sized for the applause. generous, gorgeous, and occasionally due on the first of the month.
self_questions: which grand promise is currently collecting interest?

rows.title: luck loves your entrance
rows.body: your opportunities come from being noticed. the right person in the audience, the host who remembered you, the room you almost didn't walk into. showing up shiny has paid your bills more than once.
self_questions: what break came from simply being seen?

rows.title: you fix moods instead of holding them
rows.body: when someone you love is hurting, you reach for the joke, the plan, the pep talk. sitting quietly in someone's sadness feels like doing nothing. sometimes the joke saves them. sometimes they just needed you to sit.
self_questions: who needed you to sit still with them?

rows.title: the polite no
rows.body: you're agreeable right up until someone tries to steer you. then they meet the steel under the sway. you'll hear anyone out. you'll obey no one.
self_questions: when did you learn that softness could protect sovereignty?

rows.title: here to build what remains
rows.body: you're here for the standing things. institutions, works, structures that hold weight after you've left the site. your life force runs on purposeful work, and the proof of you will still be load bearing in fifty years, which is exactly how you wanted it.
self_questions: what are you building that will still be standing?

rows.title: focus is tidal
rows.body: your attention drifts and returns on its own schedule. forcing it to stay produces nothing, riding the tide produces your best work. the trick was never discipline. it was learning the timetable.
self_questions: when does your focus reliably come in?

rows.title: the helper
rows.body: you help. even when nobody asks. fixing, explaining, showing up with the thing someone needed. it's one of the most natural things about you. just watch that the helping doesn't become hiding.
self_questions: who do you always help even when nobody asks?

rows.title: the unjust outcome haunts
rows.body: unfairness, to you or to anyone, disturbs something structural in you. you re-litigate old injustices at night, decades later, still finding for the plaintiff.
self_questions: what old injustice does your night court still hear?

rows.title: a mile wide
rows.body: your excess is scatter. ten open doors, none walked fully through. sometimes the breadth is the actual wisdom. sometimes it's the world's most interesting way to avoid the one deep thing.
self_questions: which open door deserves your whole walk through it?

rows.title: wanderlust heart
rows.body: you fall for horizons. the person from somewhere else, the taste of elsewhere, the love that comes with a passport and no itinerary. beauty, to you, is the wide open, and your heart has always had a window seat.
self_questions: what faraway thing did you fall for completely?

rows.title: the overpromise
rows.body: your excess is horizon-sized commitment. the plan assumed the best case, the calendar assumed there were two of you. your reach writes checks your hours cash late, and everyone's learned to add a buffer.
self_questions: what did you promise at horizon size?

rows.title: the un-lonely solitude
rows.body: your own company actually suffices. days alone pass without the ache other people report having. the door is open. it's just not waiting.
self_questions: what do days alone give you that company can't?

rows.title: you say a third of what you know
rows.body: information is currency and you don't overspend. in most conversations you're holding cards nobody knows you have, not from deceit, from habit. the full inventory has never been shown to anyone.
self_questions: what do you know that you've never mentioned?

rows.title: older than your years
rows.body: people have read you as mature since you were a kid. the responsible one. the one who gets it. the funny thing about capricorn rising is it runs backwards. life gets lighter as you get older, not heavier.
self_questions: when did you first get treated as older than you were?

rows.title: you free what you love
rows.body: your love comes without cages. no scripts, no roles, no becoming someone else to stay. people are most fully themselves around you, and that freedom is precisely why the real ones never leave.
self_questions: who is most themselves around you?

rows.title: everything lands on you first
rows.body: events hit you personally before they hit you in context. the canceled plan, the short reply, for one second all of it feels aimed at you. the second passes. it also always happens.
self_questions: what landed on you today that had nothing to do with you?

rows.title: anger comes out as truth
rows.body: your fury arrives as the brutally honest speech. the sermon nobody requested, delivered anyway, containing at least one thing everybody needed to hear and nobody thanks you for.
self_questions: what sermon did you deliver that aged well?

rows.title: thriving in hard soil
rows.body: your best growth happened in your worst conditions. the difficult city, the lonely year, the job that almost broke you. comfort has never taught you anything. you distrust it slightly for that.
self_questions: what did the hardest soil grow in you?

rows.title: banks for the river
rows.body: saturn sits in your boundlessness, teaching the ocean to hold a shape. structure never came naturally, boundaries even less, and every routine you keep was built like a levee, deliberately, against your own current. the discipline you have is handmade, and it's the reason your gifts reach anyone at all.
self_questions: what structure did you build against your own current?

rows.title: the celebration engine
rows.body: you'll find the occasion. a small win, a tuesday, someone's half birthday. people think you're frivolous until they realize their best memories of the year mostly have you in them.
self_questions: what are you celebrating this week, and who's invited?

rows.title: old things, kept well
rows.body: the vintage watch, the friendship from 1998, the restaurant that hasn't changed since before you were born. time is your quality certificate, and nothing under a decade old has fully earned your trust yet.
self_questions: what old thing do you love that time certified?

rows.title: lit means both scales full
rows.body: at full vitality, the harmony includes you. peace you're inside of, finally, too, not only the peace you're managing for everyone else. when your own scale gets filled, your light doubles.
self_questions: what would peace that includes you look like?

rows.title: the chase is honest
rows.body: you pursue openly. no games, no playing cool, no manufactured distance. wanting something and hiding the wanting feels like lying, so you never learned how.
self_questions: what are you openly chasing right now?

rows.title: restless in paradise
rows.body: things can be genuinely good and you'll still feel the itch. it confuses people who love you. it's not ingratitude. it's just that your compass never fully powers down.
self_questions: how do you explain the itch to someone who doesn't have it?

rows.title: romance as an art form
rows.body: you love love itself. the rituals, the anniversary remembered, the table set for two with intention. courtship is a craft to you, and you practice it long after the courting technically ended.
self_questions: what romance ritual do you keep alive?

rows.title: the late harvest
rows.body: your material life blooms late and holds. what others got at twenty five, you got at forty, built better, on land you actually own, and it has never once wobbled.
self_questions: what came late to you that came built to last?

rows.title: chosen care charges you
rows.body: tending your people, when it's chosen and not extracted, generates energy instead of spending it. the full table you cooked for leaves you fuller than the quiet night alone.
self_questions: what caring actually gives you energy back?

rows.title: teachers everywhere
rows.body: the cab driver, the podcast, the stranger at the wedding, the country you visited once. your education never had walls. some of your best thinking is built from sources no curriculum would admit to.
self_questions: who taught you something they'll never know they taught?

rows.title: behind your own door
rows.body: there's a version of you that only exists past your own front door. softer, weirder, unguarded. most people never meet them. the ones who have know they saw something rare.
self_questions: who's met that one?

rows.title: a hostile room closes the mind
rows.body: you cannot think clearly where you don't feel safe. criticism in the air, tension at the table, and your sharpest thoughts pack up and leave. people have mistaken the shutdown for having nothing to say.
self_questions: where does your thinking work best?

rows.title: luck lives in the routine
rows.body: your good luck doesn't arrive as lightning. it arrives through showing up. the routines, the small work, the days nothing special happens. that's where your growth actually compounds. keep showing up to them.
self_questions: what small routine has quietly changed your life?

rows.title: read as antisocial
rows.body: your absence from the scene gets mistaken for disliking people. you like people fine, one at a time, with the door closed and the phones down.
self_questions: who thinks you hate parties when you just love conversations?

rows.title: memory keeps the feeling
rows.body: you remember the mood of the book, not the title. the shape of the conversation, not the words. your archive is impressionist, all color and light, and somehow you can navigate by it anyway.
self_questions: what do you remember perfectly except for the facts?

rows.title: seeing through the veil
rows.body: you clock the fake instantly, the trend, the pitch, the performed emotion. your own veil taught you to see everyone else's. it's lonely, being this hard to fool.
self_questions: what do you wish you could unsee?

rows.title: feelings like weather
rows.body: your emotions arrive fast, loud, and honest. anger, joy, hurt, all of it hits at full volume and then passes like weather. you don't really do grudges, holding one takes patience and the feeling's usually already gone. people who sulk for weeks genuinely confuse you.
self_questions: what feeling burns through you the fastest?

rows.title: the lesson is enough
rows.body: saturn teaches you worth the long way. security, money, solid ground, none of it came free, and the lean seasons you knew still audit your decisions. what you've built since is real precisely because you built it against that wind.
self_questions: what did the lean years teach you that plenty never could?

rows.title: lit means rooted
rows.body: at full vitality you're deep in a place, hands in real work, nothing rushed, everything held. the settled life other people fear is your brightest possible setting, and you've always known it.
self_questions: what would fully rooted look like for you?

rows.title: you feel out loud
rows.body: you don't know what you feel until you say it. talking is how you process, and your best people are the ones who let you think out loud without needing it to make sense yet. silence isn't peace for you. it's usually a sign something's stuck.
self_questions: who do you call to find out what you feel?

rows.title: delivery decides what you hear
rows.body: a true thing said cruelly bounces off you. a half-formed thing said kindly gets a full hearing. the package and the contents were never separate in your mind, and harsh people lose you before they finish being right.
self_questions: what truth did you reject because of how it arrived?

rows.title: isolation dims the light
rows.body: too long without input, without dialogue, without the crackle of another mind, and your light goes grey. you were never built for the sealed room, and the sealed room knows it.
self_questions: how long have you been without a real exchange?

rows.title: anger becomes a plan
rows.body: fury gets filed, scheduled, and executed. the response arrives weeks later as a completed fact, and by then it isn't revenge, it's just the new arrangement.
self_questions: what response did you schedule instead of scream?

rows.title: discipline squared
rows.body: your work ethic has a work ethic. the systems, the checklists, the maintenance of the maintenance. what others call excessive, your results call thorough, and your results keep winning the argument.
self_questions: what does your discipline maintain that nobody sees?

rows.title: precision wounds the closest
rows.body: the accuracy that wins you arguments lands as coldness on the people you love. right and wounding turned out not to be exclusive, and you learned it the expensive way.
self_questions: when were you right in a way that still cost you?

rows.title: the theater of romance feels hollow
rows.body: the chase, the drama, the staged proposals of it all. you watched that play once and quietly put it down. steady and unphotographed was always the actual prize.
self_questions: what does real love look like to you, minus the show?

rows.title: creating without an audience
rows.body: your best work happens unwatched, and staying unwatched doesn't bother you. the making was the whole transaction. the showing was always optional.
self_questions: what's in your drawer that's finished and unshown?

rows.title: it leaks as the forbidden shelf
rows.body: the taboo topic, the occult tab, the thing everyone else won't look at directly. your search history reads like a séance, and you wouldn't have it any other way.
self_questions: what's on your forbidden shelf right now?

rows.title: confidence is assumed
rows.body: people read you as sure of yourself on days you're anything but. the outside broadcasts steady no matter what's happening in there. it means you rarely get checked on. the ones who look fine the loudest get asked the least.
self_questions: when did you last look confident while falling apart?

rows.title: luck comes as introductions
rows.body: your breaks are always warm handoffs, never cold applications. the person who knew the person, the name mentioned in the right room while you weren't there. people carry your luck to you.
self_questions: who said your name in a room that mattered?

rows.title: the quiet exquisite
rows.body: your taste is precise. the perfect seam, the clean line, the understated thing done exactly right. loud beauty loses to correct beauty every time, and you can spot correct from across the store.
self_questions: what do you own that's quietly perfect?

rows.title: the fear of the drop
rows.body: failure was never abstract for you. letting down the people counting on you is the nightmare with a permanent room, and it has never once checked out.
self_questions: who are you most afraid of dropping?

rows.title: peace is the need
rows.body: your nervous system runs on harmony. when your people are okay, you're okay. tension in the house means you can't rest until it's smoothed, even when it has nothing to do with you. other people's conflict lands in your body like it's yours.
self_questions: whose fight are you still carrying?

rows.title: effort as devotion
rows.body: your drive expresses as work. you fight for the things you love by fixing them, maintaining them, improving them past reason. the labor is the loyalty.
self_questions: what do you fight for by fixing it?

rows.title: never enough in the vault
rows.body: you're hungry for enough, and enough keeps moving. the number, the cushion, the proof of worth. you've hit targets that were supposed to end the wanting, and the wanting just renegotiated.
self_questions: what number was supposed to end this?

rows.title: it leaks as comparison
rows.body: other people's houses, salaries, ease. you case everyone's security like a burglar who only steals feelings. their enough always looks calmer than yours.
self_questions: whose enough do you keep measuring against?

rows.title: here to go first
rows.body: there's a reason you exist, and it's ignition. you're here to start what others will finish, to walk into the untouched thing and make it begun. your life force runs on firsts. when you're initiating, you're lit from the inside. inside someone else's plan, the pilot light gutters.
self_questions: what are you here to start?

rows.title: the why-it-matters mind
rows.body: your brain files everything under the big picture. details only stick if they connect to something that matters, and once you see the point, you've basically got it. you learn in leaps, and the leaps are usually right.
self_questions: what did you understand in one leap that others built stepwise?

rows.title: you fall for ideas
rows.body: other people have hobbies. you have obsessions. a subject grabs you and suddenly it's forty tabs and a documentary at 1am. learning is genuinely romantic for you. that's rare.
self_questions: what idea are you a little bit in love with right now?

rows.title: built for the ones after
rows.body: your work is designed to outlast you. systems, communities, standards others will stand on without ever knowing your name. saturn's best offer is anonymous permanence, and you took the deal without blinking.
self_questions: what are you building that will outlive your name?

rows.title: unbreakable under siege
rows.body: your endurance in the dark is the gift. what would end other people, you metabolize into force. every siege you've survived came out the other side as capability.
self_questions: what siege made you stronger instead of smaller?

rows.title: the body knows first
rows.body: your feelings show up as symptoms before they show up as thoughts. appetite changes, sleep goes weird, your shoulders climb. by the time you realize you're upset, your body's known for a week.
self_questions: what is your body telling you right now?

rows.title: the confession magnet
rows.body: seatmates, baristas, near strangers, they tell you things. real things. something in your face says safe deposit box, and everyone has valuables.
self_questions: what do you do with everything you're given?

rows.title: novelty runs the meter
rows.body: your interest bills by freshness, and steady things have lost to interesting strangers before. the renewal isn't automatic. the loves that lasted learned to keep surprising you, or you learned to keep looking, and one of those is a skill worth choosing.
self_questions: what steady thing lost your attention to something shiny?

rows.title: helpful is your handshake
rows.body: your first instinct with new people is to be useful. fix the wifi, carry the thing, send the link. it's how you say hello before you're ready to say anything real. some people never notice that's what it was.
self_questions: how do you help instead of saying what you feel?

rows.title: comfort looks weird on you
rows.body: your self-soothing makes no sense to outsiders. a documentary about bridges, a 2am wikipedia spiral, reorganizing a spreadsheet. the niche thing works precisely because it's yours. never let anyone normalize your coping.
self_questions: what's the weird thing that reliably fixes your mood?

rows.title: the late great partnership
rows.body: your best relationships arrive late and last forever. the early ones were coursework, credit given for attendance. the late ones are the degree, and you earned it.
self_questions: what did the early ones teach that the late one gets?

rows.title: action is your oxygen
rows.body: doing generates your energy instead of spending it. the begun project, the moving body, the decision made before breakfast. you don't rest into vitality. you move into it.
self_questions: what motion brings you back to life?

rows.title: 3am knows you
rows.body: your best thinking happens in the quiet hours. so does your worst. the same room holds both. you've done more work on yourself at night than anyone will ever see.
self_questions: what does your 3am brain keep coming back to lately?

rows.title: skepticism is the front gate
rows.body: new ideas don't just walk into your head, they get vetted. the shiny trend, the miracle method, the guy with the course, all of it waits outside while you check credentials. slow to adopt, almost never fooled.
self_questions: what trend did you rightly wait out?

rows.title: contagious courage
rows.body: your boldness recruits. people join fights they'd never have started because your banner makes winning look plausible. half your causes have a second wave you inspired and never met.
self_questions: who joined a fight because you made it look winnable?

rows.title: the feelings run underground
rows.body: people read you as detached because the feelings don't surface where anyone can see them. they run under the floor like pipes. everything's felt. it's just felt in a room nobody's been invited to.
self_questions: what did you feel deeply this week that nobody saw?

rows.title: the mind thinks in pictures
rows.body: your thoughts arrive as images, moods, whole shapes, and translating them into sentences is the hard part. you understand things fully before you can say how. linear thinkers show their work. yours doesn't come with steps.
self_questions: what do you understand completely but can't explain?

rows.title: the general's gift
rows.body: under real pressure you become the one everyone follows without discussion. command is your fire's mature form, and crises keep proving it. the field promotes you every time.
self_questions: when did a crisis put you in charge without a vote?

rows.title: the antenna
rows.body: your role is receiving what's coming before others feel it, and translating it down. every group you've belonged to got its future a little earlier because you were in the room, saying the thing three years too soon.
self_questions: what are you picking up right now that others can't hear yet?

rows.title: home is the charger
rows.body: you can be social, even great at it, but it spends you. your own space, your own things, your own quiet puts the charge back. the door closing behind you at the end of a long day is one of your favorite sounds.
self_questions: what does your version of recharging look like?

rows.title: your love appreciates
rows.body: everything you commit to compounds. the marriage, the craft, the friendship, all worth more each year, like you only know how to invest. loving you is a long position, and everyone holding it knows.
self_questions: what love of yours is worth more now than when it started?

rows.title: here to warm the room
rows.body: your shine is generative. it grows things in other people, courage, joy, permission to be bigger. you're here to be a source, the way a hearth is a source, and the rooms you've warmed remember the temperature long after you've left them.
self_questions: what grows in people when you're around?

rows.title: honesty arrives first
rows.body: the true thing is out of your mouth before the polite version finishes loading. you've apologized for deliveries but rarely for content. people learn to come to you when they want it straight, and brace when they don't.
self_questions: when did the truth cost you and you'd still say it again?

rows.title: fierce over soft
rows.body: your tenderness shows up as defense. someone hurts a person you love and you feel it like a personal declaration of war. you protect first and cuddle later, maybe.
self_questions: who protects you back?

rows.title: it leaks as the resume reflex
rows.body: you introduce yourself by function. years get measured in output. vacations feel like theft from a boss who is, on inspection, also you.
self_questions: who are you when nobody asks what you do?

rows.title: luck talks to you
rows.body: your opportunities arrive as conversations. the chat at the party that became the job, the reply that became the friendship, the dm that became the whole chapter. your network was built by accident and it works on purpose.
self_questions: what conversation turned into a door?

rows.title: growth through service
rows.body: your expansions arrive when you're useful. every big door in your life opened because you solved something real for someone. being needed was never your trap. it was your road.
self_questions: what problem did you solve that opened everything after?

rows.title: the rebel's fire
rows.body: your drive activates against systems, not people. rules that make no sense, authority that didn't earn it, the way it's always been done. your anger is principled, detached, and weirdly cheerful, and it has dismantled more structures than anyone credits.
self_questions: what structure did you quietly dismantle?

rows.title: no neutral reactions
rows.body: people either lean in or step back from you. almost nobody stays lukewarm. you've stopped taking it personally. the intensity does the sorting before you say a word.
self_questions: who leaned in when everyone else stepped back?

rows.title: changing your mind is renovation
rows.body: updating a belief is structural work for you, not redecorating. it happens, but it needs real evidence, delivered patiently, possibly twice. people mistake the slowness for stubbornness right up until you turn out right.
self_questions: what's the last belief you actually renovated?

rows.title: power, held cleanly
rows.body: all that schooling in control made you someone who can hold power without misusing it, which is rarer than any talent. saturn made sure you'd respect what you fought to keep. you do.
self_questions: what power do you hold that you've never once abused?

rows.title: the fear of sounding wrong
rows.body: behind your careful speech is an old dread of getting it wrong out loud. you over-prepare for conversations other people wing, and the preparation has never once felt optional.
self_questions: what conversation did you rehearse that others would have winged?

rows.title: you teach permission
rows.body: people watch you live differently and realize they're allowed to. your life is someone's proof of concept. the strangeness you stopped apologizing for became somebody's map.
self_questions: who is living freer because you went first?

rows.title: the overcommit reflex
rows.body: you say yes to more beginnings than one life can finish. the graveyard of started things is real. so is everything the starting taught you, and the ratio is better than it looks from inside.
self_questions: what did you start that you're ready to officially release?

rows.title: the crusade skips home
rows.body: you'll ride for strangers' justice and miss the small battle your own life needed fought. the dishes of your own kingdom pile up while you liberate someone else's.
self_questions: what small fight at home needs the crusader?

rows.title: luck hides in details
rows.body: your breaks come from being the one who noticed. the error caught, the clause actually read, the small fix that made you indispensable. your luck looks like attention and pays like magic.
self_questions: what did noticing earn you?

rows.title: other people's depths pull you
rows.body: their secrets, their finances, their psychology, their locked rooms. you study people the way some people study languages, and you're fluent in several nobody taught you.
self_questions: whose depths are you currently reading?

rows.title: the heart on a delay
rows.body: you feel things about three days late. in the moment you handle it, hold it together, do what needs doing. the feeling arrives later, alone, usually at night. people think you're unmoved. the bill just comes due on a different schedule.
self_questions: what hit you days after it happened?

rows.title: distance can dodge
rows.body: the principled detachment sometimes ducks a fight that needed your actual heat, in the room, that day, with your voice shaking. analysis has occasionally been a very smart hiding place.
self_questions: what fight needed your heat and got your theory instead?

rows.title: the spotlight's verdict
rows.body: being seen always meant being judged, and some old judgment still runs security at your stage door. every appearance gets cleared through it, even now, even after everything.
self_questions: whose old judgment still checks your tickets?

rows.title: useful love
rows.body: you don't say i miss you, you say i fixed it. affection through favors, care through competence. words feel flimsy next to a solved problem.
self_questions: what would it cost you to just say the feeling out loud?

rows.title: warm to everyone, close to few
rows.body: you're equally kind to the best friend and the barista, which is beautiful and also confusing. people can't tell if they're special to you. some of them really are. they just can't tell.
self_questions: who's special to you and doesn't know it?

rows.title: betrayal keeps its receipts
rows.body: you can forgive a lot, but broken trust gets a permanent file. you might stay friendly, you might even stay close, but a door quietly locked and the key is gone. some people never noticed which moment did it.
self_questions: whose key is gone, and do they know?

rows.title: a language nobody taught you
rows.body: money and security might feel like a language you had to learn alone. like everyone else got a class you missed. you're more fluent than you think. you learned it the expensive way.
self_questions: what did you figure out about money that nobody taught you?

rows.title: the unbought maker
rows.body: no applause dependency means nothing can be purchased from you with praise. your work stays pure and your love stays honest. that's rare currency. spend it slowly and only where it's real.
self_questions: what has being unflatterable protected you from?

rows.title: research is a trance
rows.body: you sit down to check one fact and surface four hours later, three levels deep, holding the org chart of a company you'd never heard of. the deep dive isn't a method, it's a gravity.
self_questions: what rabbit hole took your last free evening?

rows.title: the cornerstone
rows.body: your role is what others build on. teams stabilize where you stand, families organize around your steadiness, whole efforts become possible because you're under them. cornerstones don't get applause. they get permanence.
self_questions: what is built on top of you?

rows.title: unshakeable, eventually
rows.body: the ground you stand on now can't be pulled, because you laid every stone yourself. security you build with your own hands is the only kind saturn certifies, and yours is certified.
self_questions: what can't be taken from you because you built it?

rows.title: no walls in there
rows.body: your heart has no walls. movies wreck you, songs from the wrong year wreck you, other people's pain gets in like it's yours. you feel more in an afternoon than some people manage in a month. none of it has ever learned to stay outside.
self_questions: when did you last cry about something that wasn't yours?

rows.title: curation is affection
rows.body: your playlists, your gift choices, your recommendations are all edited hard. being included in your curation is the actual intimacy. the people you love get your selects, never your drafts.
self_questions: who gets your curated best?

rows.title: fix first, feel later
rows.body: someone cries and your brain hands you a toolkit. solutions, links, a plan by morning. the feeling part of you shows up later, usually alone, usually in the car.
self_questions: when did fixing become safer than feeling?

rows.title: itchy feet
rows.body: people can see the restlessness on you. the tab always half open on somewhere else, the plans that assume motion. some call it flighty. standing still was never the plan anyway.
self_questions: where does the itch want to take you right now?

rows.title: showing up is the love language
rows.body: you say i love you by being there. every time, on time, for years. the airport pickup, the moving day, the 3am call answered. words feel flimsy to you. attendance is the vow.
self_questions: who knows they can count on you without asking?

rows.title: the disciplined mind
rows.body: your intelligence is trained, not just quick. the systems, the notes nobody else takes, the study habits that never retired. you outlearned the naturally clever by simply not stopping.
self_questions: what did you master by outlasting the talented?

rows.title: ease arrives late
rows.body: permission to relax came years behind the competence. you could always do the thing. enjoying doing it took another decade, and it's still arriving in installments.
self_questions: what can you finally enjoy that you could always do?

rows.title: slow to fall, slow to leave
rows.body: your heart doesn't do quick. you warm up slowly, and then you stay warm for years. even leaving things that hurt takes you a long time. it's just your speed.
self_questions: who have you loved the longest?

rows.title: you mother the room you lead
rows.body: in any team you're running, you end up tending feelings, not just tasks. people bring you their stuff because the role reads as safe. leadership, for you, has always included the caretaking.
self_questions: who on your team leans on you?

rows.title: worth on installment
rows.body: believing you deserve things came slowly, receipt by receipt. you've had to earn your own sense of value the way you earned everything else, and the payments took years.
self_questions: when did you start believing you deserved what you'd built?

rows.title: the knowing arrives without evidence
rows.body: you know things before you can prove them. a feeling about a person, a dream that turns out to be right, a no in your body with no argument attached. you've overridden it before and regretted it every time.
self_questions: when did the feeling know before you did?

rows.title: the underground fire
rows.body: your drive is total and patient. you want things with a depth that would scare people if you showed it, so you don't. your anger doesn't explode, it descends, and it can wait years for the exact right moment. what you truly aim at doesn't escape.
self_questions: what did you want so completely that you told no one?

rows.title: the x-ray
rows.body: you read what's underneath. the tension behind the smile, the request inside the compliment, the goodbye rehearsing itself inside a hello. it makes you impossible to fool and hard to relax around, until someone earns the private you. then they discover the strange truth: nobody is more loyal than the one who trusts almost no one.
self_questions: who has earned the private you, and how?
what did seeing too much cost you?

rows.title: delight on demand
rows.body: you can access joy instantly. no buildup, no ceremony, no right conditions required. the first bite, the first chord, the first sight, all at full volume. that immediacy is a gift most people meditate for years to fake.
self_questions: what delighted you today, instantly?

rows.title: the deliberate warrior
rows.body: because your courage costs something, it's never reckless. when you finally move, it's real, weighed, and worth following. people trust your leaps precisely because they watched you consider them.
self_questions: who follows you because your courage is considered?

rows.title: read as faithless
rows.body: your distance from religion gets mistaken for emptiness. the faith is there, old and load bearing. it just never needed a building, a book, or a membership.
self_questions: who assumes you believe in nothing?

rows.title: the channeled sea
rows.body: water with banks becomes a river, and rivers move things. your structure doesn't cage the ocean, it aims it. everything you've built lets the boundless in you actually arrive somewhere, for someone.
self_questions: where does your river arrive now?

rows.title: the clever hands
rows.body: you think with your hands. fixing, making, kneading, typing, untangling the necklace everyone else gave up on. control matters to you, not over people, over craft, over the small physical world, because when your hands are busy your mind finally goes quiet. skill is your language and competence is your love letter.
self_questions: what did your hands learn to do before your mouth learned to say?
where does your mind go when your hands are busy?

rows.title: the late victory
rows.body: you win slowly, permanently. not the sprint, the campaign. your victories take years and arrive quietly, but they never get reversed, because you built them on ground you tested first. people with faster flash pass you constantly, early. then a decade goes by and you're the one still standing, holding everything you said you'd hold, wondering where they went.
self_questions: what long game are you in the middle of right now?
what's a slow win of yours that nobody watched happen?

rows.title: home travels with you
rows.body: you left the nest earlier than most, one way or another, and it never broke you the way everyone expected. roots, homeland, the family address, all of it sits loose on you. home lives in a pocket you carry, and every actual house is just weather.
self_questions: when did you realize home wasn't a place for you?

rows.title: the healer of details
rows.body: your calling lives at the level everyone else skips. the exact dosage, the specific clause, the small hinge the whole door turns on. things fail or thrive at that level, and you're one of the few stationed there.
self_questions: what small hinge are you tending that holds a big door?

rows.title: the wide angle heart
rows.body: you find it easy to care about everyone and harder to be needed by one person at close range. causes, communities, the whole species, no problem. a single human's daily emotional weather pointed directly at you is the advanced course.
self_questions: who taught you to care up close?

rows.title: luck arrives as resources
rows.body: your breaks show up in physical form. the good deal, the inherited tools, the right material at the right moment. abundance finds you as stuff, land, and terms, and it always seems to know your address.
self_questions: what resource arrived exactly when you needed it?

rows.title: the private struggle
rows.body: you'd rather suffer efficiently in private than worry anyone. by the time people learn what you went through, it's past tense, handled, narrated with a shrug.
self_questions: what are you currently handling alone that's actually heavy?

rows.title: tending feeds you
rows.body: watering, maintaining, the slow care of real things. it doesn't drain you the way it drains others. it charges you, and your most restful days are secretly full of quiet work.
self_questions: what do you tend that tends you back?

rows.title: faith, load tested
rows.body: saturn sits on your beliefs. easy optimism was never issued to you, and every philosophy you hold got there by surviving your own doubt. your faith is structural, stress tested, built from the rubble of beliefs that failed. it holds weight because it has held weight.
self_questions: which belief survived your doubt and earned its place?

rows.title: the stray magnet
rows.body: animals cross rooms for you. so do lost tourists, crying strangers, new kids, anyone unmoored. something in you reads as shelter from across a street.
self_questions: what stray, human or otherwise, changed your life?

rows.title: the fixer under fire
rows.body: in a crisis your competence becomes a weapon. while everyone panics, you triage. the calm list-making in the emergency room of any disaster, that's your fire, and it saves things.
self_questions: what did your calm competence save?

rows.title: loss doesn't land like loss
rows.body: broken, stolen, gone. you grieve objects for about an hour. people find your speed eerie. you find their year of mourning a lamp eerie right back.
self_questions: what loss surprised you by not hurting?

rows.title: pride prolongs the war
rows.body: apologizing first feels like abdication, so some conflicts ran months longer than the disagreement deserved, both thrones waiting for the other to bow.
self_questions: which war is still running on pride alone?

rows.title: counting as a nervous habit
rows.body: balances get checked like weather. tallies run under conversations. the math of your security is always open in a background tab, and closing it has never once occurred to you.
self_questions: what are you counting right now?

rows.title: the becoming is the point
rows.body: fed right, this hunger is an engine most people would kill for. you were built to keep becoming, and the ones who arrive tend to stop. the next honest becoming will feed you. the next costume won't.
self_questions: what's the next honest becoming, not the next costume?

rows.title: the same, again, please
rows.body: you like your favorites on repeat. same order, same songs, same people. newness is fine but sameness is where you actually rest.
self_questions: what's something you never get tired of?

rows.title: the feeling becomes fuel
rows.body: pain doesn't just sit in you, it converts. heartbreak becomes the best work of your life, anger becomes discipline, grief becomes depth. your heart runs a refinery, and nothing that enters comes out unused.
self_questions: what pain did you turn into something?

rows.title: the heart wants witnesses
rows.body: your feelings are big and they want to be seen. not by everyone, by the ones who matter. quiet love isn't quite enough, you need it shown, said, celebrated a little. when someone really notices you, your whole system settles.
self_questions: who really sees you?

rows.title: hungry to win
rows.body: you're starving for the overcome. the rival outworked, the illness beaten, the impossible load carried. you don't relax in peace, you go looking for the next opponent. because who even are you without a fight.
self_questions: who are you between battles?

rows.title: the weighing mind
rows.body: every question gets both sides in your head, argued fully, by you, against you. it makes you fair to a degree most people can't manage. it also means what do you think is genuinely the hardest question you get asked.
self_questions: what are you weighing right now that others find obvious?

rows.title: hungry to become
rows.body: there's a version of you that you've been chasing your whole life. bigger, realer, finally arrived. every reinvention was a lunge at it. the hunger is for existing at full size, and no size has felt full yet.
self_questions: what would full size even look like?

rows.title: pretense dims you
rows.body: sustained small talk, performed harmony, rooms full of fine. your light can't run on artificial anything, and every hour of pretense drains what an hour of truth would have doubled.
self_questions: what pretense is draining you right now?

rows.title: read as cold about family
rows.body: your looseness with roots gets misread as not caring. the caring is real. it just never needed proximity to survive, and that confuses people who measure love in miles.
self_questions: who thinks distance means you love them less?

rows.title: feelings get sorted first
rows.body: you need to understand a feeling before you'll say it out loud. it goes through processing, gets named, checked, filed, and only then shared. by the time you tell someone you were hurt, you've already handled most of it alone.
self_questions: what are you still sorting before you'll say it?

rows.title: you feed people instead of telling them
rows.body: when words feel too risky, the care comes out as food, rides, remembering the little things. you've said i love you a thousand times without once using the sentence. the ones paying attention got the message.
self_questions: who did you feed this week instead of telling them?

rows.title: cases become patterns
rows.body: one person's story is, to you, a data point in something larger. your mind zooms from the individual to the structure automatically. it makes you brilliant at diagnosis and occasionally late to just say that sounds hard.
self_questions: what pattern did you spot that others took personally?

rows.title: the early declaration
rows.body: you say it out loud before it's safe to. the dream, the verdict, the thing everyone's thinking. your conviction arrives early and fully formed, and it's contagious, people find themselves agreeing with you before they've checked why. you're water that decided on its direction. being unconvinceable is your superpower and, occasionally, your blindfold.
self_questions: what declaration are you currently living inside?
when has your certainty been wrong in a way that taught you something?

rows.title: younger than the paperwork
rows.body: people guess your age wrong in the same direction every time. something in the face stays curious, and curiosity photographs young. you'll be asking questions at ninety and it'll still be working.
self_questions: what keeps you young that has nothing to do with age?

rows.title: making things fixes your mood
rows.body: a bad feeling wants a project. cooking, drawing, building the playlist, anything made with your hands moves the feeling through. creation is your pressure valve.
self_questions: what did you last make to feel better?

rows.title: calm in the emergency
rows.body: when everything collapses, you get quieter and clearer. the panic that floods everyone else never got your number. people remember who you were the day it all went wrong.
self_questions: who remembers your calm from their worst day?

rows.title: your feelings have an audience
rows.body: your emotional life happens where people can see it. at work, in your role, in public. privacy about your state was never really on the menu, so you learned to feel in front of witnesses.
self_questions: who saw your last hard day?

rows.title: the fast tongue fights
rows.body: your weapon is words. arguments are fencing, wit is the blade, and you can dismantle a position in two sentences without raising your voice. your drive sparks in three directions at once and somehow still catches things.
self_questions: when did two sentences do the work of a whole war?

rows.title: lit means nothing numbed
rows.body: at full vitality, you're alive to all of it. nothing anesthetized, nothing skipped, the whole current running through you and changing what it touches. allowed fully, you're incandescent, and you know exactly which moments proved it.
self_questions: when were you last incandescent?

rows.title: hungry for the other
rows.body: you're starving for the one across the table. the partner, the mirror, the us. alone has never once felt like enough, and you've bent yourself into shapes for the promise of two. the hunger is ancient, and it's picky about nothing.
self_questions: what has the promise of two cost you?

rows.title: the observer's seat
rows.body: at every gathering there's a moment where you drift to the edge and just watch. it's your favorite seat in any house. from there people make sense, patterns show up, and you love everyone a little better at that range.
self_questions: what do you see from the edge that you miss up close?

rows.title: love without edges
rows.body: your taste is oceanic. you fall for souls, songs, strangers on trains, all of it fully. beauty moves you to actual tears on a regular schedule, and love has never once arrived in you at a moderate volume.
self_questions: what beauty last brought you to tears?

rows.title: aim it at real dragons
rows.body: fed right, this hunger fixes what's actually broken. the debt, the health, the injustice sitting right there. you were built for battles. the only audit that matters is which ones deserve you.
self_questions: which fight actually deserves you?

rows.title: the kids find you
rows.body: children and the childlike are drawn to you, and your feelings light up around them. some of your purest moods happen at their eye level.
self_questions: who brings out the kid in you?

rows.title: here to connect
rows.body: you're here as a bridge. between people, between ideas, between worlds that would never have met without you. your life force is exchange itself, and every real conversation charges the battery. the connections you make will outlive every other thing you do.
self_questions: what have you connected that changed both sides?

rows.title: the no shows before you say it
rows.body: when you're done, your whole body says so. arms, jaw, the way you settle into the chair like a building. people push anyway and then act surprised the wall was load bearing.
self_questions: what's a no you held that someone kept testing?

rows.title: luck wears disguises
rows.body: your opportunities arrive dressed as endings. the layoff that freed you, the loss that redirected you, the no that turned out to be the door. your luck has never once looked like luck on arrival.
