self_questions: what ending turned out to be a beginning in costume?

rows.title: the light packer
rows.body: you own less than anyone expects and miss none of it. moving house takes you an afternoon and a friend with a sedan.
self_questions: what's the least you've ever happily lived with?

rows.title: trust has floors
rows.body: strangers get the lobby. friends get a floor or two. almost nobody's seen the top of the building. you built it that way.
self_questions: who's been the furthest in?

rows.title: your mood has a plus one
rows.body: your emotional weather tracks your closest person. their good day lifts you, their bad day lands on you. solo feelings almost feel unfinished, like half a conversation.
self_questions: whose day sets yours?

rows.title: calm makes you suspicious
rows.body: still water bores you into mischief. you've stirred a peaceful stretch just to have something real to swim in, and called it honesty while doing it.
self_questions: when did you last stir still water on purpose?

rows.title: read as wasting potential
rows.body: your indifference to advancement drives ambitious people quietly crazy. they see squandering. you see a race you already ran, somewhere they can't check the records.
self_questions: who can't forgive you for not wanting more?

rows.title: the counting habit
rows.body: the account. the progress. the proof. some part of you is always checking the number, and the number never quite says done. noticing the checking is half of loosening it.
self_questions: what number do you check the most?

rows.title: comfort can become a moat
rows.body: your taste for the pleasant builds walls without meaning to. same restaurant, same order, same beloved everything. some new delights have been waiting years for the drawbridge.
self_questions: what new pleasure is waiting outside the moat?

rows.title: you count heads
rows.body: at any gathering you're quietly tracking who's eaten, who's cold, who got weird after the third drink. hosting happens in your body whether it's your house or not. people feel taken care of around you and can't say why.
self_questions: who taught you to watch the room like that?

rows.title: agreeing to keep moving
rows.body: you nod along to things you don't agree with because the alternative is a whole thing. people walk away certain you're on their side. later you're annoyed at them for believing you.
self_questions: what have you agreed to out loud but never inside?

rows.title: the feeling moves faster than the name
rows.body: by the time you've described what you feel, it's changed. yesterday's crisis reads like someone else's diary. people accuse you of being fickle. your weather just has a faster cycle.
self_questions: what upset you last week that's already gone?

rows.title: anger arrives as politeness
rows.body: when you're furious you get formal. the warmth drops ten degrees, the courtesy gets crisp, and the observant get chills. your coldest 'of course' has ended entire dynamics.
self_questions: who has felt your polite fury?

rows.title: you learn by doing it wrong once
rows.body: theory primes you, but the mistake teaches you. one wrong attempt with your own hands beats three tutorials. your competence is built out of corrected errors, each one filed and never repeated.
self_questions: what mistake taught you the most?

rows.title: principles with maintenance schedules
rows.body: your values get upkeep. re-examined, stress tested, lived even when inconvenient, especially then. most people have opinions. you have infrastructure, and you inspect it.
self_questions: which principle did you keep when it cost you?

rows.title: for them, always
rows.body: you'll accept things for yourself that you'd go to war over for your people. threaten someone you love and the claws come out completely, and everyone's always surprised.
self_questions: who would you fight for that you'd never fight for yourself over?

rows.title: you dissolve into who you love
rows.body: you take the shape of your relationships. their music becomes your music, their moods set your thermostat, and one day you look up and can't find where they end and you start. love shouldn't require a missing person report.
self_questions: what did you like before you loved them?

rows.title: the pattern outlives the facts
rows.body: you forget where you read it, who said it, what the study was called. the shape of the idea stays. your mind keeps blueprints and throws away receipts.
self_questions: what do you know for sure without remembering how?

rows.title: you collect other people's problems
rows.body: coworkers, clients, the stranger in line, everyone's issues end up on your desk. the helping is real. so is the pile, and nobody's tracking its weight but you.
self_questions: whose problem are you carrying that was never assigned to you?

rows.title: trust the wordless compass
rows.body: your knowing works without a map, and the only wrong turns you've ever taken were overriding it for someone else's doctrine. it's allowed to be this simple. it always was.
self_questions: when did overriding your knowing cost you?

rows.title: guilty resting
rows.body: sitting still feels like theft. someone might need something, somewhere. rest only counts for you if everyone else is fed, settled, and asleep first.
self_questions: who taught you that your rest comes last?

rows.title: past the applause
rows.body: attention never fed you the way it feeds others. compliments, spotlights, being adored, all of it arrives and just sits there. you make things, love people, and skip the part where the room confirms it mattered. that receipt was collected long ago.
self_questions: what did you make that nobody ever saw, happily?

rows.title: connection charges you
rows.body: company, partnership, the good table with the right people. you literally light up in twos and small circles, and your solo brilliance was always brighter with someone to hand it to.
self_questions: which company reliably lights you up?

rows.title: the polite shell
rows.body: new people get warmth, but it's the outer layer. friendly, funny, completely sealed. you decide slowly who gets past it and the deciding happens somewhere you can't rush. the shell has a door and you're the only one with the schedule.
self_questions: how long does it take someone to actually get in?

rows.title: flowers for yourself
rows.body: you don't wait to be given nice things. you buy the flowers, book the table, light the candle on a wednesday. someone has to treat you right and you decided early it might as well be you.
self_questions: when did you stop waiting to be treated well?

rows.title: intensity seeking intensity
rows.body: mild interests, mild people, mild plans, you respect them the way you respect furniture. what pulls you is whatever burns: projects, places, people with their own fire.
self_questions: what's burning in your life right now, and is it warming or consuming?

rows.title: weird path, real wealth
rows.body: you were never going to build worth the normal way. your money, your voice, the value you make, it's all supposed to look different from how you were raised. the strange route isn't a detour. it's the route.
self_questions: what's the most you-shaped way you've ever earned something?

rows.title: the open face
rows.body: you read as free. big laugh, honest eyes, the friend who's probably up for it. people assume you're doing great because your face defaults to yes. it's mostly true. and the mostly does a lot of quiet work.
self_questions: what does the open face keep people from asking about?

rows.title: the question behind the question
rows.body: people ask you one thing and you answer the thing they actually meant. the stated question is a door, and you were always going to walk through it. it unsettles people pleasantly, or just unsettles them.
self_questions: what is someone really asking you lately?

rows.title: wisdom by syllabus
rows.body: your grasp of the big questions is studied, not vibed. the theology, the philosophy, the actual books read to the end. you did the coursework others just quote at parties.
self_questions: what did you actually read that everyone else just cites?

rows.title: anger goes strategic
rows.body: no scenes, no raised voice. you go quiet, and the quiet is planning. by the time you respond, it's not a reaction anymore, it's a decision.
self_questions: what response did you plan instead of react?

rows.title: warm on arrival
rows.body: your first move with people is generosity. big hello, real attention, you make people feel like the party started when they walked in. it costs you something but you'd never bill for it.
self_questions: who lights up when you show up?

rows.title: you absorb instead of study
rows.body: forcing yourself to learn fails. soaking works. you sit near a subject long enough and one day you just have it, like language in a childhood home. nobody watched you learn it, including you.
self_questions: what did you learn without ever studying it?

rows.title: you teach people how to be held
rows.body: your presence shows people what care actually feels like. someone learned belonging at your table, and they carried the recipe into their own life. that's teaching, even if no one called it that.
self_questions: who learned what care feels like from you?

rows.title: the velvet fight
rows.body: your drive wears gloves. you fight through negotiation, charm, alliances, the strongly worded conversation over coffee. open combat feels vulgar to you, and you've won most of your wars before the other side knew one had started.
self_questions: what war did you win without a single battle?

rows.title: luck comes from the edges
rows.body: your breaks arrive from the margins. the online community, the acquaintance of an acquaintance, the group nobody took seriously until it mattered. your center is fed by your edges, always has been.
self_questions: what came to you from the edge of your world?

rows.title: lit means always learning
rows.body: at full vitality your life has permanent curiosity and people to share it with. the day you're brightest is the day you learned something and told someone before sunset.
self_questions: what did you learn today, and who gets to hear it?

rows.title: learned once, kept forever
rows.body: your mind doesn't rent knowledge, it buys. what you truly learn stays learned, the skill from fifteen years ago still runs clean. slow acquisition, permanent storage.
self_questions: what can you still do that you learned decades ago?

rows.title: you teach people to look
rows.body: your comfort with the unspoken gives others courage to face their own. people have had their realest conversations with you, about things they'd never said out loud. you make the deep end feel survivable.
self_questions: who faced something because you didn't flinch?

rows.title: the root puller
rows.body: you can't leave the bottom of things alone. why the family is like this, why the relationship really ended, why you are the way you are. where others accept the surface, you dig, and you'll tear up a whole garden to examine one root. it makes you the most honest excavator people know, and it means your life has ruins in it, structures you demolished because the foundation was a lie.
self_questions: what are you digging at right now?
what did you tear down that you sometimes miss?

rows.title: you outlast
rows.body: your strategy in any fight is endurance. you win by still being there, still steady, still holding position after everyone else's energy ran out. sieges break against you.
self_questions: what did you win just by not leaving?

rows.title: feelings need a witness
rows.body: you process best in dialogue. a feeling alone in your head just circles, but say it across a table and it starts making sense. you don't need advice. you need the other chair filled.
self_questions: who fills the other chair for you?

rows.title: the favorite
rows.body: you want to be chosen, specifically, out loud. not liked. chosen. being one of many is your quiet nightmare, and being someone's favorite is the safest you ever feel.
self_questions: who made you feel chosen, and what did they do?

rows.title: one true sentence
rows.body: when you do speak, it lands with a weight practiced talkers can't buy. that's the trade you came in with. keep saying only the real ones, and they'll keep landing.
self_questions: what's the truest sentence you've said this year?

rows.title: lit means giving light
rows.body: at full vitality your shine is in service, warming people, growing courage, funding joy. the sun doesn't hoard, and neither do you at your brightest. give it away and there's somehow always more.
self_questions: who needs your light this week?

rows.title: the escape and the path
rows.body: your excess is drift. surrender and avoidance wear the same coat, and sometimes you can't tell which one you've got on until years later. one of them grows you. the other just moves you.
self_questions: right now, are you surrendering or avoiding?

rows.title: growth through the different
rows.body: you expand by breaking the pattern. the unconventional path, the community of strangers, the idea that shouldn't work. your luck lives outside the standard plan, and every time you've trusted your weird, the weird has paid.
self_questions: when did the unconventional path pay off?

rows.title: your space is your mood ring
rows.body: the state of your home and the state of your head are the same fact. clutter climbs, mood drops. cleaning the kitchen has fixed more of your bad days than talking ever has.
self_questions: what is your space saying right now?

rows.title: growth lives in commitment
rows.body: you expand inside real partnership, not around it. the deep contract, professional or personal, is where your becoming happens. half-in has never grown you an inch.
self_questions: what are you half-in on that deserves all-in or out?

rows.title: the warmth is a few doors in
rows.body: first meetings get the composed version. polite, capable, a little reserved. the softness and the jokes live further inside, and only people who stick around find them. everyone who does is surprised.
self_questions: who was surprised when they finally got to know you?

rows.title: office games look like theater
rows.body: the politics, the credit-grabbing, the jockeying for the good chair. you see every move clearly and can't be bothered to audition. it's a play you can watch without joining.
self_questions: what game does everyone play that you sat out?

rows.title: maximum or nothing
rows.body: you rest like it's a competition and work like the building's on fire. the middle setting on you is broken, or maybe was never installed.
self_questions: what would a medium day even look like for you?

rows.title: everything can delight you
rows.body: your taste has no gate. the gas station snack, the overheard sentence, the weird fact, the b-side. you find something lovable in nearly everything, which means your days have more doors to joy than most lives get.
self_questions: what tiny weird thing delighted you lately?

rows.title: you speak fluent whoever
rows.body: you shift to match the person in front of you. vocabulary, pace, even posture. it's automatic. sometimes you catch yourself mid conversation and wonder which version this one is.
self_questions: who gets the version closest to the middle?

rows.title: wanting over having
rows.body: the chase is the best part and you know it. the wanting is bright and specific. the having is nice, then quiet, then you're looking at the horizon again.
self_questions: what would it take to enjoy the having half as much as the hunt?

rows.title: the mind listens for tone
rows.body: you hear how it was said louder than what was said. information arrives with a feeling attached, and the feeling gets filed as part of the fact. your thinking is never neutral, and it catches what neutral minds miss.
self_questions: what did you hear today underneath the words?

rows.title: wanting before words
rows.body: you know what people want before they ask. sometimes before they know. it makes you generous at your best and dangerous at your tiredest, and you know which days are which.
self_questions: what do you do with what you see on the tired days?

rows.title: the devil's advocate lives in you
rows.body: someone states a position and your mind instantly builds the counter, even when you agree with them. it's not contrarianism, the other side just materializes. you've argued against your own team more than once, on principle.
self_questions: when did you argue a side you didn't even hold?

rows.title: depth is the whole portfolio
rows.body: while everyone's collecting contacts, you've been compounding three friendships into something unbreakable. in the end, that's the portfolio that pays out. yours already is.
self_questions: what have your few given you that a network never could?

rows.title: love as co-adventure
rows.body: affection, for you, is doing the big thing together. the trip, the leap, the shared story you'll tell for decades. souvenirs are your love letters, and your best relationships have luggage tags.
self_questions: what adventure was really a love story?

rows.title: already enough
rows.body: stuff never got its hooks in you. you can lose things, lend things, leave whole apartments behind, and feel lighter each time. the security everyone's stacking, you carry in a different pocket. nothing you can hold has ever held you up.
self_questions: what did you leave behind that everyone said you'd miss?

rows.title: hungry for the deep
rows.body: surface anything starves you. you want the secret, the intensity, the transformation, the rooms behind the curtains. you'd rather be destroyed and rebuilt than comfortable, and your history shows you've meant it.
self_questions: what did you walk into knowing it would remake you?

rows.title: you fight for the drowning
rows.body: your aggression only fully activates on behalf of the helpless. the victim, the animal, the one being laughed at across the room. then a person nobody's met shows up in your body.
self_questions: who woke up the fighter in you?

rows.title: you get noticed
rows.body: you don't blend. you've tried, it doesn't take. you walk in and the room does a small quiet recalibration around you, even when you're dressed down and saying nothing. being seen is your default setting. the only choice you get is what they see.
self_questions: what do you hope people see first?

rows.title: hungry to be heard
rows.body: you're starving for your words to land. the message, the platform, the room that finally listens. you'll say it louder, sharper, again. somewhere back there someone didn't listen, and you've been correcting it ever since.
self_questions: who didn't listen, back at the start?

rows.title: the one who carries
rows.body: you take the heavy stuff without being asked. other people's grief, family secrets, the emotional luggage nobody claims at the end of the night. you carry it so quietly that people forget you're carrying anything at all. but your arms are full, and have been for years.
self_questions: what are you carrying that was never yours?
who checks the weight on you?

rows.title: waiting is the hardest feeling
rows.body: you can handle bad news. it's the not knowing that wrecks you. limbo makes you want to force an answer, any answer, just to end the suspense. you've blown things up early just to stop waiting for them to maybe fall.
self_questions: what did you end early just to stop the waiting?

rows.title: small errors, big verdicts
rows.body: a typo in the pitch and you quietly doubt the whole company. the detail is never just the detail to you, it's a sample of everything you can't see. harsh, maybe. wrong, rarely.
self_questions: what small thing made you distrust something big?

rows.title: your voice is for something
rows.body: fed honestly, this hunger makes messengers. write the true thing, say the real version. one person actually hearing you beats a thousand impressions, and deep down you know which one you've been chasing.
self_questions: what's the true thing you haven't said plainly yet?

rows.title: privacy as armor
rows.body: you know everyone's story and tell almost none of yours. it's not shyness. information is intimacy, and intimacy is earned, slowly, in installments.
self_questions: who knows your story past the first installment?

rows.title: the standing bench
rows.body: people bring you their disputes because your verdicts hold. being trusted with fairness is a lifetime appointment, and you earned the bench one just call at a time.
self_questions: whose disputes come to you for judgment?

rows.title: the soft first read
rows.body: strangers tell you things. on planes, in lines, at parties they meant to leave early. something in your face says this one's safe, and people hand you their whole story before they know your last name. you didn't ask for the job. the face applied for it without you.
self_questions: what's the biggest thing a stranger ever told you?

rows.title: growth through the deep end
rows.body: you expand through what most people avoid. the crisis, the shadow, the truth under the truth. your biggest growth came out of your hardest chapters, and you came out transformed, never just intact. depth is your direction of increase.
self_questions: what dark chapter grew you the most?

rows.title: friends are the medicine
rows.body: your mood is communal. a night with your people repairs things solitude can't touch. chosen family is a load bearing wall in your emotional house, and you know exactly who's in it.
self_questions: which friends actually restore you?

rows.title: first through the door
rows.body: you walk into rooms like you've already decided. before you say a word people read you as someone who moves first and figures it out later. quick, direct, a little impatient with slow. strangers either match your pace or step out of the way.
self_questions: what do people get about you in the first ten seconds?

rows.title: beauty you can hold
rows.body: your loves are physical. the real book, the cut flower, the ceramic with the right heft. digital delights never fully count for you. if it can't be held, it's only half owned.
self_questions: what do you own that you love holding?

rows.title: nostalgia doesn't visit
rows.body: old photos, childhood streets, the ancestral whatever. others weep at the slideshow, you observe it. the past is a country you fully emigrated from, papers and all.
self_questions: what does everyone else miss that you simply don't?

rows.title: headlines, not footnotes
rows.body: give you the point first. context, background, methodology, all of it can come later if you ask, and you usually won't. you extract the essence of a meeting in the first four minutes and spend the rest waiting.
self_questions: what's the shortest version of what you're working through right now?

rows.title: after the show
rows.body: there's a version of you after the room empties. quieter, tired in a way that surprises people who only know the shine. the performance is real. but so is the person who sets it down at the door.
self_questions: who gets the after-the-show you?

rows.title: the deep taste
rows.body: you don't like things, you're claimed by them. attraction arrives as fate, total and specific, and mild interest isn't in your emotional range. the things you love, you love at a depth that would frighten them if they knew.
self_questions: what claimed you the moment you met it?

rows.title: you teach compassion
rows.body: people are gentler after knowing you. your default mercy resets what others think normal is. someone forgives more easily because they once watched you do it without ceremony.
self_questions: who softened because of you?

rows.title: the critique kills the mood
rows.body: you notice the flaw mid-delight. the crooked frame at the lovely dinner, the typo in the sweet note. your editor doesn't clock out for pleasure, and it has cost you full enjoyment of things that deserved it.
self_questions: what did the flaw steal from you that the whole deserved?

rows.title: you take your time on purpose
rows.body: people mistake your pace for hesitation. you're just not answering until you've actually decided. the answer takes a minute. it also doesn't change after.
self_questions: when has waiting saved you?

rows.title: visible from everywhere but home
rows.body: the people closest to you have gotten the leftovers of your ambition for years. strangers get the polished summit self. the dinner table gets the phone face. they've noticed. they've been noticing.
self_questions: who's been getting your leftovers?

rows.title: the big version first
rows.body: your mind draws the vision before the floor plan. the grand shape of the thing arrives complete and thrilling, and the details are somebody's problem, occasionally yours, ideally later.
self_questions: what vision are you carrying that has no logistics yet?

rows.title: the fear of dissolving
rows.body: losing the plot, the schedule, the self. part of you knows exactly how easily you could drift entirely, and the knowing is what keeps a hand on the wheel at all times.
self_questions: what keeps your hand on the wheel?

rows.title: the title was supposed to be it
rows.body: each promotion bought about six weeks of arrival. then the office got quiet and the next rung cleared its throat. the ladder has never once run out of ladder.
self_questions: how long did the last title feed you?

rows.title: everyone's home
rows.body: people rest near you. it's the thing you do without doing anything. friends land on your couch, at your table, in your calendar, and leave heavier with food and lighter everywhere else. caring for people isn't a task you perform. it's the shape of you. the question nobody asks is where you go to rest.
self_questions: where do you go to rest, actually?
who feeds you?

rows.title: the deflection
rows.body: someone asks how you're doing and you're answering about someone else within a sentence. your own news feels less urgent. it isn't.
self_questions: what's your actual answer to how are you, today?

rows.title: here to shelter
rows.body: you're here to make safety exist in the world. the fed table, the held space, the person who got through the year because you were in it. your life force is belonging, given and received, and everything you build is secretly a roof.
self_questions: who got through something because you existed?

rows.title: growth for the many
rows.body: your expansions are biggest when they're not just for you. the cause, the community, the thing others will use after you. scale is your direction, and your growth has always traveled in groups.
self_questions: what are you growing that others will use?

rows.title: peace keeps getting scheduled
rows.body: you'll rest when the house is done, when things calm down, after this one stretch. the calm is permanently one project away, and the projects have noticed they're immortal.
self_questions: what has to finish before you're allowed to rest?

rows.title: service without a scoreboard
rows.body: you help without tracking credit. thanked or not, seen or not, the help costs you the same and gives you the same. the ledger everyone else keeps was never issued to you.
self_questions: who have you helped that never knew it was you?

rows.title: the next person glows
rows.body: new people arrive lit up, finally the answer. the glow is half them and half your hunger's projector, and telling the two apart has taken you years each time.
self_questions: who did you light up that couldn't hold it?

rows.title: romance as a stage
rows.body: you've loved being adored more than you've fully admitted. the falling is the drug, the being-fallen-for especially. the settled part of love keeps reading like a demotion from the opening night.
self_questions: what happens for you when the falling part ends?

rows.title: quick saves the day
rows.body: your speed of thought in a crisis untangles what force can't touch. the talked-down disaster, the negotiated exit, the right words at the exact wrong moment. that's real rescue work.
self_questions: what crisis did you talk everyone out of?

rows.title: sad makes you restless
rows.body: when you're down, you don't curl up. you look at flights, plan escapes, reorganize your whole life at 1am. movement is how you outrun the feeling. sometimes it works. sometimes the feeling was in the luggage.
self_questions: what are you planning your way out of right now?

rows.title: the untangler
rows.body: knots, bureaucracy, other people's messes. you have unusual patience for tangled things and a small private satisfaction every time one comes loose.
self_questions: which tangle in your life right now would respond to patience?

rows.title: you teach hope
rows.body: people leave conversations with you believing more is possible. the belief is contagious and you're the carrier. some of them built whole lives on a possibility you handed over casually.
self_questions: who caught hope from you?

rows.title: your own anger is the scary one
rows.body: you can handle everyone else's hard feelings, it's yours that feel dangerous. anger especially. it gets swallowed, softened, translated into something more polite, and it doesn't disappear. it just waits.
self_questions: where does your anger actually go?

rows.title: read as unambitious
rows.body: your peace with not-winning gets mistaken for not caring about the work. the work matters completely. the podium was the part you never saw the point of.
self_questions: who confuses your calm with not caring?

rows.title: the quiet ledger
rows.body: you keep score without meaning to. who called last, who compromised, who's been carrying more. you'd never present the invoice out loud, but the ledger's accurate, and it's why some resentments feel so old.
self_questions: what's the oldest entry in your ledger?

rows.title: overlooked hurts worse than insulted
rows.body: you can survive criticism, you can even use it. what actually wounds you is being forgotten. the uninvited, the unnoticed, the effort nobody mentioned. indifference cuts you deeper than any insult ever has.
self_questions: when did being overlooked hurt more than it should have?

rows.title: it leaks as the conversion pitch
rows.body: when you believe, everyone hears about it. the enthusiasm arrives with reading lists. your convictions have always come with a newsletter, and your friends have always been subscribed involuntarily.
self_questions: what are you currently converting people to?

rows.title: sharpened by the worst thing
rows.body: the hardest thing that ever happened to you is also where your vision comes from. you'd never say you're grateful for it. but you see things now that you couldn't before.
self_questions: what do you see now that you couldn't see before it happened?

rows.title: hungry to dissolve
rows.body: you're starving for the exit. sleep, oceans, altered states, the place just past the edge of yourself. being a person all day is the job, and dissolving is the paycheck you keep chasing. the hunger is for release, and it has never been picky about the door.
self_questions: what are you trying to take a break from being?

rows.title: work hidden in play
rows.body: people underestimate you because you make it look pleasant. they miss that the ease is the skill. you've done your hardest work on a couch, laughing, and let them think it was luck.
self_questions: what have you achieved that nobody clocked as work?

rows.title: harder on you than anyone
rows.body: the calm surface hides a running commentary that talks to you in ways you'd never let anyone talk to a friend. nobody outside can hear it. from out there you just look composed.
self_questions: what would change if you graded yourself like you grade people you love?

rows.title: growth by leaping
rows.body: you grow by starting before you're ready. the courses half finished, the moves made on instinct, the thing launched on a random tuesday. every real expansion in your life began with a jump that looked premature and wasn't.
self_questions: what leap grew you the most?

rows.title: friendly from a distance
rows.body: everybody likes you and almost nobody can place you. you're warm in a way that keeps a fixed distance, present in the room and slightly beside it at the same time. people describe you as cool, easy, a little unreadable. the crowd feels closer to you than you feel to the crowd.
self_questions: when do you feel most like you're watching the room instead of in it?

rows.title: growth through others
rows.body: your expansion is relational. the partner, the collaborator, the mentor, the ally. you grow in pairs, and every major chapter of your life has a co-author. alone you're fine. accompanied, you're exponential.
self_questions: who has been a door for you?

rows.title: no small feelings
rows.body: you don't do mild. a song is either skipped or played forty times. a person is either family or a stranger. people call it intense. you call it honest.
self_questions: where did you learn that halfway wasn't worth doing?

rows.title: the sibling thread
rows.body: your emotional life was shaped side by side. siblings, cousins, the kids on the street. those early bonds set a template you still run, in loyalty and in old friction both.
self_questions: who grew up alongside you?

rows.title: the put-together face
rows.body: people hand you responsibility on sight. keys, plans, secrets, the group chat that actually organizes things. something about you reads as this one has it handled, and you mostly do, which keeps the applications coming. competence is your first impression and your longest running role.
self_questions: when did you get promoted to responsible one, and did anyone ask you first?

rows.title: the crowd of one
rows.body: you can feel alone in any group and complete when actually alone. solitude isn't your backup plan, it's your native country. company is the foreign travel.
self_questions: what does solitude give you that no person ever has?

rows.title: you learn by grazing
rows.body: depth is optional, coverage is instinct. a bit from a video, a thread, half an article, a conversation, and suddenly you can hold your own on the topic. the buffet approach looks unserious and works anyway.
self_questions: what do you know a surprising amount about for no reason?

rows.title: the crowd already emptied
rows.body: networks, scenes, the big rooms everyone's working, you've got no pull toward any of it. your circle is three people and it's finished, the way a house is finished. the many never fed you. somewhere before this you had the crowd, and you left the party early on purpose.
self_questions: when did you know the crowd wasn't for you?

rows.title: you teach by being proof
rows.body: your existence demonstrates that the long way works. someone stayed patient with their own climb because they watched yours pay off. you're evidence, walking around.
self_questions: who kept climbing because you proved the summit exists?

rows.title: read as careless with money
rows.body: your ease gets mistaken for irresponsibility. the wanting is just quiet in you. money passes through your hands without ever sticking to your heart.
self_questions: who worries about your relationship with money more than you do?

rows.title: anger becomes articulation
rows.body: your fury comes out as devastating clarity. you've never thrown a punch. you've ended entire positions in a group chat before lunch.
self_questions: what's the sharpest thing you ever said while calm?

rows.title: luck actually likes you
rows.body: your near-misses and last-minute saves are statistically suspicious. the door held, the money arrived, the stranger helped. optimism keeps getting funded, and you keep reinvesting.
self_questions: what saved you at the last minute?

rows.title: distraction is the painkiller
rows.body: when something hurts, you open a new tab. a podcast, a project, a person, anything with enough signal to drown the ache. it works great right up until the quiet, where everything you skipped is waiting.
self_questions: what are you currently drowning out?

rows.title: endings hit the body
rows.body: goodbyes make you physically tired. moving out, last days, funerals, even finishing a show. endings land somewhere under your ribs and stay a while.
self_questions: what ending are you still digesting?

rows.title: here to carry meaning back
rows.body: you're here to seek, and then to come back and tell. the scout of significance, sent ahead to find what matters and return with it. your life force runs on the quest itself, and the people you've handed meaning to are your actual body of work.
self_questions: what meaning did you find and hand to someone?

rows.title: joy travels with you
rows.body: your capacity for enjoyment is enormous and portable. you can find the fun in a parking lot, the story in a delay, the feast in a gas station. wherever you land, the good time was apparently in your bag.
self_questions: where did you find joy that had no business being there?

rows.title: the listening one
rows.body: you learned the world through your ears. stories, confessions, the thing under the words, you catch it all, and people sense it, which is why strangers hand you their lives within an hour. your knowledge came from listening at doors the world didn't know were open. the cost of hearing everything is that you're rarely the one being heard.
self_questions: who actually listens to you the way you listen?
what's the most important thing you ever learned by staying quiet?

rows.title: you clock everything
rows.body: the typo, the loose thread, the thing slightly off about the plan. you see it all within seconds and say maybe a tenth of it. people would be alarmed by the full list. the restraint is the kindness.
self_questions: what did you notice today and let slide?

rows.title: the band, not the solo
rows.body: your best work happens in ensembles, the team, the group chat, the scene. alone you're skilled. synced with others you're something else entirely.
self_questions: which group brings out your best tempo?

rows.title: small perfect things
rows.body: the exact right pen. the correctly ripe pear. the shirt that fits like math. your capacity for micro-delight is a renewable joy that big-gesture people can't access, and it never runs out of stock.
self_questions: what small perfect thing made your week?

rows.title: every fact becomes a stance
rows.body: information doesn't stay neutral in you for long. you learn a thing and within a week it's a position, a philosophy, a hill. your mind converts data into belief automatically, and belief is where your energy lives.
self_questions: what did you recently learn that's already a conviction?

rows.title: your face reacts before you do
rows.body: you can feel it happen. someone says something slow or wrong and your face has already answered. you've lost arguments you never meant to start because your eyebrows got there first.
self_questions: when did your face say something you didn't mean to?

rows.title: renunciation muscle
rows.body: you can give things up cleanly, habits, ambitions, even people, when you decide they're done. not coldly. completely. your letting-go is so quiet people mistake it for never having held on.
self_questions: what did you renounce that others still don't know about?

rows.title: the faraway look
rows.body: people wave a hand in front of your face and ask where you went. you went somewhere real. processing happens for you in a place that looks like absence from the outside. you always come back with something.
self_questions: where do you go when you go?

rows.title: built for the good part
rows.body: you're unembarrassed about pleasure, and that's rarer than it sounds. rest, romance, the long lunch, the nap taken without apology. people around you grind and apologize and defer their lives. you enjoy yours now, on purpose, and quietly teach everyone near you that it's allowed.
self_questions: what pleasure have you never once felt guilty about?
who taught you that enjoying things was suspicious?

rows.title: romance as weather
rows.body: you flirt the way other people make small talk. harmless, ambient, half unconscious. life just tastes better with a little charge in the air.
self_questions: where's the line between your charm and your armor?

rows.title: strength you can build on
rows.body: your steadiness under pressure is structural. in a crisis, people anchor to you without asking, and the anchoring holds. being load bearing is your fire's quiet form.
self_questions: who anchors to you when things shake?

rows.title: the silver lining reflex
rows.body: you find the upside before the shock even passes. it's genuine, not performance, your mind just runs toward light. the only cost is that some things needed to be sat with first, and you'd already reframed them by lunch.
self_questions: what did you find the bright side of a little too fast?

rows.title: conflict doesn't show
rows.body: you can be furious and pouring someone tea. the face stays pleasant long past the point where the feeling did. people find out you were upset weeks later, secondhand, and can't believe it.
self_questions: how would anyone know you were angry?

rows.title: read as unavailable
rows.body: your completeness gets mistaken for walls. there are no walls. there's just no vacancy sign either, and some people can't tell the difference.
self_questions: who mistook your wholeness for a locked door?

rows.title: love as pure choice
rows.body: when you do partner, it's the cleanest kind. no rescue, no filling, just wanting. that's whole choosing whole, and it's the rarest offer on any market. never let anyone file it under settling.
self_questions: what would make you choose someone, needing nothing?

rows.title: words leave marks
rows.body: the clever cut lands deeper than you meant. you forgot it by dinner, they kept it for years, and you found out much later what your speed had done.
self_questions: what did you say lightly that someone carried heavily?

rows.title: principled to the point of pain
rows.body: when you believe in something you'll suffer for it, the stand at work, the boycott, the hard conversation everyone else avoided. comfort has never once outvoted conviction in you.
self_questions: what conviction has cost you the most?

rows.title: the clean cut
rows.body: when you're done with someone, you're done. no slow fade, no maybe later. people are shocked by how cleanly you can close a door you held open for years.
self_questions: is there a door you closed too fast?

rows.title: the closed door
rows.body: people feel you before they understand you. there's a weight to your presence that shows up ahead of your name, and strangers respond to it without knowing what it is. you read everyone within minutes. nobody returns the favor because you've made sure they can't.
self_questions: what do you know about people that they never told you?

rows.title: the diplomat wins wars
rows.body: your negotiated victories leave no bodies and both sides intact, still able to work together after. history calls that statesmanship, and it's harder than swinging ever was.
self_questions: what did you resolve that everyone else would have escalated?

rows.title: the weighed word
rows.body: saturn sits on your voice. speaking up, being heard, trusting your own intelligence, all of it carried extra gravity from the start. you learned to choose words like they cost money. now every one of yours lands, and the rooms that once talked over you lean in.
self_questions: when did your words start landing?

rows.title: the self-made wind
rows.body: you built yourself, and you know it. whatever you were given, the thing people meet now is your own construction, assembled far enough from home that nobody could take credit. independence isn't a preference for you, it's load-bearing. you can bend to almost anything, sway through almost anyone's storm, because your roots are in yourself and travel with you.
self_questions: what did you build entirely without help, and who have you never told?
what would it mean to let someone hold something for you?

rows.title: here to make it last
rows.body: you're here for permanence. to take what's fragile and make it stand, to be the reason something survived. your life force runs on tending. the garden, the craft, the people made secure because you existed. the world keeps things because people like you keep them.
self_questions: what exists because you kept it alive?

rows.title: play keeps you alive
rows.body: your heart requires actual fun on a schedule. games, silliness, delight for its own sake. adult life keeps filing it under optional and your mood keeps proving otherwise.
self_questions: when did you last properly play?

rows.title: lit means your own mountain
rows.body: at full vitality, the summit is one you chose, not one assigned. duty picked freely is your brightest state, and the difference between carrying and climbing is entirely about who selected the mountain.
self_questions: did you choose your current mountain?

rows.title: don't rush the feeling
rows.body: when someone demands to know what you feel right now, you go blank. your emotions move at their own speed and pressure just seals the vault. give you a day and you'll come back with the truth.
self_questions: who gives you the time you need?

rows.title: define your own summit
rows.body: free of the ladder, you get to pick a mountain nobody's ranking. meaning over metrics, chosen work over assigned climbing. most people can't afford that choice. you were born paid up.
self_questions: what mountain would you pick if nobody was scoring?

rows.title: ignition isn't arrival
rows.body: the instant pull has a short warranty, and you've mistaken the spark for the destination more than once. some fires were only ever meant to be matches, and you married a few of them anyway, in one way or another.
self_questions: what spark did you follow further than it deserved?

rows.title: far away feels like home
rows.body: distance restores you. other countries, other languages, being a stranger somewhere. your heart resets in places where nobody knows your name, and it never fully resets where everybody does.
self_questions: which faraway place holds a piece of you?

rows.title: the plain days test you
rows.body: love's unglamorous stretches feel like the show closing. the sweatpants era, the logistics era, the nothing-planned era. some real love got mistaken for dying just because the lighting got ordinary.
self_questions: what good love felt dull only because it stopped performing?

rows.title: the unbreakable word
rows.body: once you truly commit, the thing is already done, it just hasn't happened yet. your promises have a different density than most people's. everyone who knows you knows it.
self_questions: what commitment are you carrying that still has years left?

rows.title: vague makes you itch
rows.body: soonish is not a time. some stuff is not a quantity. probably fine is not a status. your mind runs on specifics, and conversations without them feel like walking on a floor that might not be there.
self_questions: what vague answer are you currently tolerating?

rows.title: the heavy things get left with you
rows.body: you're where people put down what they can't carry. confessions, the family secret, the thing they've told no one. you hold it well, and holding it well is why it keeps coming.
self_questions: what are you holding for someone right now?

rows.title: you don't perform urgency
rows.body: everyone around you is rushing and you're finishing your coffee. some part of you knows most emergencies are theater. the real ones you show up for. the fake ones can wait.
self_questions: what's the last emergency that turned out not to be one?

rows.title: here to thin the borders
rows.body: you're here to remind everything that it's connected. through art, through compassion, through presence that makes the line between people go soft. your life force runs on the boundless, and every border you've thinned let something through that needed to pass.
self_questions: what passed through you into the world?

rows.title: you teach courage by accident
rows.body: people watch you go first and borrow the nerve. you've started more of other people's journeys than they've ever told you. being the one who jumps is a public service you never signed up for.
self_questions: who got braver by watching you?

rows.title: fluent in letting go
rows.body: release is your native motion. endings, sleep, silence, the dissolve everyone else fears or chases, you slip in and out of it like a house key. the letting go that takes others a lifetime of practice, you do on the exhale.
self_questions: what have you released that others would still be gripping?

rows.title: the jeweled eye
rows.body: you see the design in everything, and the flaw in the design, instantly, involuntarily. rooms, outfits, sentences, lives. it makes you brilliant at making things beautiful and quietly exhausted by a world that keeps shipping first drafts. you don't just want to be seen. you want to be seen accurately, in good light, as the finished piece you're building.
self_questions: what are you designing your life to look like, and who's the audience?
what's beautiful about you that has nothing to do with effort?

rows.title: the common sense filter
rows.body: every clever idea has to pass one test in your head: would this actually work on a tuesday. elegant theories with no street value get filed and forgotten. your mind keeps its feet on the ground on purpose.
self_questions: what popular idea fails your tuesday test?

rows.title: annoying optimism
rows.body: your hope has annoyed people in dark moments. you've learned to time it better. but you never actually lose it, even when you pretend to.
self_questions: when has your hope been exactly the right thing?

rows.title: luck feels like grace
rows.body: your breaks arrive unearned and perfectly timed, from directions you weren't watching. the call, the coincidence, the stranger with exactly the thing. you've quietly stopped calling it coincidence.
self_questions: what arrived from a direction you weren't watching?

rows.title: they chase, you shrug
rows.body: people fall for you at inconvenient rates, drawn to exactly the self-sufficiency they can't crack. the pursuit puzzles you more than it flatters you, and it's never once stopped.
self_questions: why do you think they keep finding you?

rows.title: lit means work that is love
rows.body: at full vitality, craft and care are one motion. the thing you do best, done for people you can name, is your brightest state, and everyone downstream of it can feel the difference.
self_questions: who is downstream of your best work?

rows.title: the thin place
rows.body: your role is being where the border gets thin. between people, between worlds, between what's seen and what isn't. people feel more around you and can't explain it, and they seek you out at the exact moments they need the veil lifted.
self_questions: who seeks you when they need the veil thin?

rows.title: here to build peace that holds
rows.body: you're here for harmony as an achievement. bridges between people that bear weight, beauty in shared spaces, fairness that actually functions when tested. peace, where you've worked, has structure. that's the difference between your peace and a ceasefire.
self_questions: what peace have you built that actually held?

rows.title: the yes gets out early
rows.body: your face agrees before your mind votes. people see soft and assume available, and by the time you've checked with yourself you've already nodded. half your obligations were signed before you got a say.
self_questions: what did you agree to before you actually decided?

rows.title: the translator
rows.body: your function is making one world understandable to another. the expert to the beginner, the parent to the kid, this field to that one. you live at the joints of things, and the joints are where everything actually connects.
self_questions: which worlds do you stand between?

rows.title: both doors
rows.body: choosing kills you a little. the fork in your symbol is real: you want the career and the escape, the person and the freedom. you're not indecisive. you're greedy for lives.
self_questions: which door are you pretending you haven't already chosen?

rows.title: easy to like
rows.body: people warm to you in minutes. you make first meetings smooth, find the common ground, keep the conversation from ever hitting the floor. everyone leaves thinking you two really clicked. you do it so well that almost nobody wonders what you actually thought of them.
self_questions: when's the last time someone knew your real opinion in the first hour?

rows.title: the fear of handing over the keys
rows.body: being at anyone's mercy, in any currency, triggers something ancient in you. you keep escape routes in relationships that don't need them, and the routes are always current.
self_questions: which escape route could you finally close?

rows.title: sleep like a door
rows.body: you cross into sleep, dream, daydream, easily and deep. the border was always soft for you. some mornings you're not fully convinced which side you woke up on.
self_questions: what do you find on the other side of the door?

rows.title: anger arrives as tears
rows.body: fury and crying share a pipe in you, and the wires cross mid-argument, which everyone misreads as weakness right before you hold your ground anyway. wet eyes, unmoved position.
self_questions: when did you cry and still not back down?

rows.title: the harbor
rows.body: your role is where people dock in storms. they arrive wrecked and leave seaworthy, and they don't always say thank you, and they always come back. generations will describe your shelter to people who never met you.
self_questions: who docks in your harbor?

rows.title: you're everyone's shelter
rows.body: because home lives in you, you can hand it out anywhere. people feel settled around you in the middle of chaos, in airports, in waiting rooms. the portable hearth is the inheritance. share it.
self_questions: who has felt at home simply because you were there?

rows.title: the handshake
rows.body: your word is the contract. you say tuesday, it happens tuesday. flaky people genuinely confuse you, like watching someone set fire to their own money.
self_questions: when did keeping your word become your whole identity?

rows.title: secrets don't tempt you
rows.body: the hidden, the forbidden, the locked rooms that pull everyone else in. you glance and move on. mysteries feel like reruns of a show you've already seen through.
self_questions: what fascinates everyone that leaves you cold?

rows.title: you teach fairness
rows.body: people leave dealings with you knowing what being treated well feels like, and it raises their standards everywhere else. you've upgraded relationships you're not even in.
self_questions: whose standards did your fairness raise?

rows.title: the built family
rows.body: whatever family didn't come standard, you constructed. chosen people, kept traditions, safety assembled piece by piece over years. your belonging is architecture, and you were the architect.
self_questions: who's in the family you built?

rows.title: you explain it three ways
rows.body: when someone doesn't get it, you don't repeat, you rephrase. an analogy, then a diagram, then the version with their job in it. translation is a reflex, and it's why people ask you to explain things they were just told.
self_questions: who comes to you for the translated version?

rows.title: the quiet certainty
rows.body: your opinions don't require a podium. you say things once, softly, and let them find whoever's listening closely. repetition always felt like begging.
self_questions: what do you know that you've only said once?

rows.title: the hunger knows real value
rows.body: aimed right, this appetite builds actual foundations, for you and everyone you love. it just needs you to decide the number once, on paper, on purpose. otherwise it decides itself, forever, upward.
self_questions: what would you write down as actually enough?

rows.title: rich in public
rows.body: you're generous visibly, gifts, rounds, the good bottle. some of it is joy, some of it is proving something to a leaner past that still lives in you.
self_questions: what does your generosity say to your past?

rows.title: seduced by minds
rows.body: you fall for conversation. the clever reply, the reference caught mid-air, the banter that escalates into something. beauty, for you, is interesting, and boredom is the only true ugliness you've ever met.
self_questions: what's the best conversation you ever fell for?

rows.title: things grow near you
rows.body: plants, projects, people. things you tend actually flourish, and you quietly notice you're often the reason a place feels alive.
self_questions: what are you tending right now that's visibly growing?

rows.title: hungry to be special
rows.body: ordinary feels like dying to you. you're starving to be singular, unrepeatable, the one. the creations, the romances, the performances, all chasing the same certificate: proof you're not just anyone.
self_questions: who first made you feel like just anyone?

rows.title: forty tabs open
rows.body: your mind runs on parallel tracks. three interests, two conversations, a podcast underneath, and somehow it all files itself. you think in connections, this reminds you of that, and the that is never what anyone expects.
self_questions: what two unrelated things did your brain connect this week?

rows.title: the improvement trap
rows.body: your excess is endless optimizing. the thing is good, then better, then somehow never shipped. some of your growth is fully grown and waiting on your permission to be done.
self_questions: what's finished except for your permission?

rows.title: drawn to the soft-hearted
rows.body: kindness is your beauty standard. you've watched gorgeous people turn ugly in one cruel sentence, permanently, and plain people turn radiant by how they treated a waiter.
self_questions: who became beautiful to you through kindness?

rows.title: art is a love affair
rows.body: songs, films, paintings affect you like relationships. you've been changed by fiction, wrecked by an album, healed by a scene in something nobody else remembers. the art loves you back. you're sure of it.
self_questions: what piece of art changed you like a person would?

rows.title: you look like you have it handled
rows.body: that's the first thing people meet. the composed one. the capable one. older than your years, somehow. the warmth is real but it's a few doors in, and most people never learn how funny you actually are. you'd rather be respected than adored. and you usually are.
self_questions: what do people always get wrong about you at first?

rows.title: the practiced practice
rows.body: your meditation, your art, your routine, all maintained like treatment. the softest person in the room with the strictest calendar, and both things are completely true at once.
self_questions: which practice holds you together?

rows.title: the precise strike
rows.body: your drive is surgical. you don't swing wide, you find the exact weak point and press it. your anger comes out as critique, itemized, accurate, devastating. you fight with a list, and the list is correct.
self_questions: what's on the list you haven't read out yet?

rows.title: growth needs variety
rows.body: you expand in seasons of newness and stall in repetition. when you feel stuck, the fix is almost never more effort. it's new input. change the feed and the growth restarts on its own.
self_questions: what new input does your stuck place need?

rows.title: gifts with your whole chest
rows.body: your presents are events. researched, wrapped, timed for maximum wonder. you'd rather over-give than adequately give, every single time, and the faces have always been worth the budget.
self_questions: what's the best gift you ever gave?

rows.title: tears are just weather
rows.body: you cry at commercials, at kindness, at nothing you can point to. it embarrassed you for years until you noticed the tears aren't always sadness. sometimes that's just what full looks like, spilling a little.
self_questions: what made you cry recently that wasn't sad?

rows.title: sad looks like busy on you
rows.body: when you're hurting, your output goes up. more work, more projects, more usefulness. people see productivity and miss the grief powering it. your hardest seasons have some of your best results, and that's not a coincidence you love.
self_questions: what were you building the last time you were sad?

rows.title: allergic to shortcuts
rows.body: the hack, the loophole, the fake-it path. you physically can't. it's not virtue exactly, it's that unearned things sit in your hands wrong, like counterfeit money.
self_questions: what's something you did the long way that you're glad you did?

rows.title: certainty is the counterfeit
rows.body: you crave the answer so hard you've bought a few fakes, fully, cash up front. conviction felt exactly like arrival, at least twice. the real thing apparently itches more than that.
self_questions: what certainty did you buy that turned out counterfeit?

rows.title: the midwife of endings
rows.body: your role is presiding over necessary deaths. of illusions, of chapters, of old selves that finished their work. people come to you when something needs to end well, because you're not afraid of the room where that happens.
self_questions: what ending are you helping deliver?

rows.title: duty as reflex
rows.body: you take responsibility before it's assigned. the check, the plan, the heavy end of the couch, your hands are already there before the question finishes asking itself.
self_questions: what did you take on before anyone asked?

rows.title: anger has footnotes
rows.body: when you finally blow, it arrives with dates, examples, and exhibits. the case was under construction for months, and opposing counsel never stood a chance.
self_questions: what case have you been quietly building?

rows.title: quality over everything
rows.body: one perfect thing beats ten fine ones, in objects, in food, in people. you can feel cheap from across the room, and no discount has ever talked you out of the feeling.
self_questions: what's the one perfect thing you chose over ten fine ones?

rows.title: read as passive
rows.body: your silence in debates gets mistaken for having no position. you have one. defending it publicly just never made the list of things worth doing.
self_questions: what position do you hold that nobody knows about?

rows.title: the scheduled summit
rows.body: everything you want arrives, on time, later than you wanted. your life runs on saturn standard time, and for all the waiting, the deliveries have never once failed to come.
self_questions: what arrived late that arrived exactly right?

rows.title: comfort is how you love
rows.body: your care is physical. the meal cooked, the blanket brought, the favorite snack remembered. you make people comfortable because comfort is the most honest word you know for love.
self_questions: how do you say i love you without saying it?

rows.title: small talk burns
rows.body: you can survive about four minutes of weather and weekend plans before something in you starts looking for the exit or the real conversation, whichever comes first.
self_questions: what question do you wish people opened with?

rows.title: water beats stone
rows.body: your yielding wins the long game. everything hard that ever opposed you got worn smooth eventually, and you were still there, still soft, still flowing. patience is your violence.
self_questions: what stone are you currently wearing smooth?

rows.title: easy gets mistaken for shallow
rows.body: you make thinking look effortless so people assume you're skating. they don't see the reading, the connecting, the 2am rabbit holes behind the quick joke. being underestimated is annoying. it's also cover.
self_questions: what do you know deeply that people assume you only skim?

rows.title: loyalty is the romance
rows.body: devotion proven over time is your actual love language. the staying, through the ugly seasons, without being asked. grand gestures are nice. the person who's still there in year seven is gorgeous.
self_questions: whose staying was the most beautiful thing they did?

rows.title: the voice carries the feeling
rows.body: people hear your state before they hear your words. warmth, flatness, the tired edge, the whole report is in your tone. phone calls with you never needed video.
self_questions: what did your voice give away today?

rows.title: peace requires two
rows.body: you can't compartmentalize a fight with your person. it follows you into every room, sits in every meal, until it's actually repaired. nothing in your day works while the two of you don't.
self_questions: what stays broken until it's repaired with them?

rows.title: every door out gets tried
rows.body: the scroll, the sleep, the daydream, the whatever helps tonight. the exits rotate. the exiting doesn't. you've never met an escape hatch you didn't at least rattle.
self_questions: which exit is currently in rotation?

rows.title: complete arriving
rows.body: you've never been half looking for a half. alone sits easy on you, easier than it's supposed to, and partnership is something you can genuinely take or leave. it makes you strange in a world of searchers. it also makes you the one they keep finding.
self_questions: when did you notice you weren't searching?

rows.title: the mind goes to the bottom
rows.body: you don't learn topics, you excavate them. surface answers feel like insults, so you keep digging until you hit the real mechanism. what you know, you know completely. what you say is maybe a third of that.
self_questions: what have you researched to a depth nobody suspects?

rows.title: thinking out loud, with flair
rows.body: your ideas arrive dressed for the occasion. you think in stories, explain with color, and land conclusions with a certainty that makes rooms believe you. teaching a thing is how you finally own it.
self_questions: what do you explain better than the experts?

rows.title: allergic to disrespect
rows.body: you can forgive almost anything except being talked down to. condescension lands on you like a slap. you've walked away from good things over it and never once regretted the walk.
self_questions: what's the difference between your pride and your dignity?

rows.title: already through the fire
rows.body: crisis doesn't scare you the way it should. endings, losses, the deep water everyone dreads, you swim it with an old familiarity, like you drowned once and settled the matter. intensity chases other people. it nods at you in passing.
self_questions: what catastrophe left you strangely calm?

rows.title: your ideas are your children
rows.body: criticize the proposal and you'll feel it in your chest. the line between your thoughts and your self was always thin, so feedback on the work lands like feedback on the person. you defend ideas the way people defend family.
self_questions: which idea of yours can you still not hear criticized calmly?

rows.title: the harmony tax
rows.body: your excess is accommodating your way out of your own growth. some of the yeses that kept the peace were quiet nos to your own expansion. the tab for pleasant has a total.
self_questions: what growth did you trade for keeping things smooth?

rows.title: out of the race
rows.body: competition never took. rivals, rankings, the daily war everyone suits up for, you watch it like a sport you played professionally once and quietly retired from. you'll work hard, but never to beat someone. that fire came pre-extinguished.
self_questions: when did you first notice you weren't racing anyone?

rows.title: make the thing anyway
rows.body: fed honestly, this hunger is pure creation. the certificate you're starving for only gets printed one way: finish something real and sign it. ordinary made things beat perfect unmade ones, every time, forever.
self_questions: what would you finish if ordinary was allowed?

rows.title: the finished self is a gift
rows.body: because you don't need to become anyone, your energy is free in a way most people's never is. point it outward. the unbuilt self was never laziness. it was a head start.
self_questions: what could you do with the energy others spend on becoming?

rows.title: being useful settles you
rows.body: you feel best mid-task. helping, fixing, tending, serving. idle days sound relaxing and feel terrible. rest for you usually means a different kind of work.
self_questions: who or what did you tend today?

rows.title: the hesitation before the leap
rows.body: a pause lives between you and every bold move. others jump on impulse. you jump through the pause, every time, which is a different sport entirely, and a harder one.
self_questions: what's on the other side of your current pause?

rows.title: allergic to preaching
rows.body: the moment wisdom gets a podium and a price, you're gone. truth that needs marketing rings false to you automatically, and the ring has never been wrong.
self_questions: what teacher lost you the moment they started selling?

rows.title: teach the exhale
rows.body: your ease with release is medicine in a gripping world. people near you learn to let go by proximity, without a single lecture. that's a quiet ministry, and it counts more than the loud ones.
self_questions: who has learned to let go just by being near you?

rows.title: no shallow end
rows.body: you feel everything and you keep all of it. love from years ago is still warm somewhere in there, old hurts are filed with dates attached. your heart has no shallow end, everything that ever mattered is still in the water. it makes you rich in ways that sometimes ache.
self_questions: what do you still feel that everyone else moved on from?

rows.title: drawn to the dark subjects
rows.body: true crime, mysticism, death, the taboo shelf. your curiosity goes where dinner conversation won't. understanding the dark has always felt safer to you than pretending it isn't there.
self_questions: what dark subject taught you something bright?

rows.title: rootless, not lost
rows.body: you can start over anywhere. new city, new field, new self. people call it brave. to you it's just tuesday. what looks like rootlessness is actually a root system that lives inside you.
self_questions: which restart taught you that you'd always land?

rows.title: strange medicine
rows.body: your fixes are unconventional, the odd routine, the fringe practice, the advice nobody saw coming that turned out right. mainstream answers bore you. edges are where your cures live.
self_questions: what worked for you that no one would have prescribed?

rows.title: read as hard to impress
rows.body: your flatness at grand gestures gets mistaken for coldness. sincerity moves you completely. production values move you not at all, and people keep buying the wrong ticket.
self_questions: what actually moves you that no one thinks to try?

rows.title: the face people project on
rows.body: everyone sees something different when they look at you. one friend swears you're the funny one, another the wise one, a third the lost one. your face is soft in a way that takes whatever people bring to it. being seen accurately is rare for you. being seen fondly happens all the time.
self_questions: which version of you do people invent most often?

rows.title: trust arrives late
rows.body: your full trust takes years to issue and it's the real thing when it comes. the people who hold it know exactly what it cost, and not one of them takes it lightly.
self_questions: who earned the full issue, and how long did it take?

rows.title: growth follows the nest
rows.body: every time you've upgraded your home base, your whole life expanded to fill it. the space comes first, the growth moves in after. when you're stuck, look at where you live before you look at what you do.
self_questions: what would growing your home base unlock?

rows.title: the teacher changed your weather
rows.body: somewhere back there was a mentor, a grandparent, a guide whose voice still steadies you. you quote them without noticing. some of your calm is borrowed from them, permanently.
self_questions: whose voice still guides you?

rows.title: growth needs one true witness
rows.body: your deepest expansions happened because someone who mattered believed in you out loud. the mentor, the parent, the partner who said you can. being believed in is your fertilizer, and you grow to the size of it.
self_questions: whose belief in you are you still growing into?

rows.title: aimed work charges you
rows.body: labor pointed at something real generates your energy. aimless leisure drains you faster than hard work ever has, which confuses everyone who keeps prescribing you vacations.
self_questions: what aimed work restores you?

rows.title: portable home
rows.body: home isn't an address for you, it's a feeling you can pitch anywhere. give you a week and any room starts to feel like yours.
self_questions: what are the three things that make a place yours?

rows.title: respected over adored
rows.body: if you had to pick, you'd take respect over being liked. you probably picked it a long time ago without noticing. it's served you well. just check sometimes that adored is still allowed too.
self_questions: where in your life do you allow yourself to just be liked?

rows.title: the next place will fix it
rows.body: the move, the city, the apartment with better light. it genuinely helps, every time, for about three months. then the old restlessness finds the new address.
self_questions: how long did the last move last?

rows.title: consensus is a red flag
rows.body: when everyone agrees, you start looking for what they missed. not to be difficult, though it reads that way. unanimous just means unexamined to your mind, and history keeps backing you up.
self_questions: what does everyone around you agree on that you quietly doubt?

rows.title: growth needs a bigger map
rows.body: whenever life plateaus, the fix is a wider frame. new country, new field, new philosophy. you don't push through walls. you zoom out until they're small enough to step over.
self_questions: where does your map need to get bigger?

rows.title: the master's touch
rows.body: all those exacting years made your hands genuinely masterful. what you produce now carries a quality that can't be faked or rushed, and everyone who receives it knows. saturn's apprenticeship ends in mastery. yours did.
self_questions: what do you make now that only those years could have taught?

rows.title: boredom breaks your brain
rows.body: you can't absorb what doesn't spark. the dull meeting, the dry chapter, the monotone lecture, none of it goes in, no matter how important. interest is a hard requirement of your comprehension, and it always was.
self_questions: what important thing can you just not make yourself learn?

rows.title: little trips fix you
rows.body: a drive, a walk to the corner, twenty minutes anywhere else. you don't need the big getaway, you need out of the room. small changes of scene do disproportionate repair on you.
self_questions: where's your short escape?

rows.title: allergic to the ladder
rows.body: every time you were supposed to climb, you wandered off toward something more interesting. the org chart has never once appeared in your dreams, and it's taken the hint.
self_questions: where did you wander when you were supposed to climb?

rows.title: the keeper of last things
rows.body: deathbeds, endings, final conversations, you can be present where others flee. something in you is at peace with conclusions, which makes you the one people want at the hardest hours.
self_questions: which ending were you present for that changed you?

rows.title: the emergency contact
rows.body: you're the first call for at least four people's disasters. flat tires, breakups, 3am spirals. you always answer. you've never once wondered if you should.
self_questions: what would happen if you didn't answer, just once?

rows.title: needing people feels like debt
rows.body: asking for help costs you something that's hard to explain. you'd rather carry it badly alone than well with assistance. leaning on someone feels like a loan you'll owe forever, so you mostly don't.
self_questions: what are you carrying alone that has no reason to be?

rows.title: growth in the light
rows.body: you expand where you're seen. the stage, the leadership seat, the room that claps. visibility is soil for you. every time you've dared to be bigger in public, life met you at the new size.
self_questions: where did being seen grow you?

rows.title: you make things beloved
rows.body: anything you care for becomes precious. the rescued plant, the thrifted chair, the friend nobody else checked on. you add sentiment like seasoning, and everything you touch ends up mattering more.
self_questions: what did you make precious that arrived ordinary?

rows.title: you turn life into occasions
rows.body: a tuesday dinner becomes a memory around you. the random thursday gets a toast, the small win gets a ceremony. people's lives are genuinely more lit because you refuse to let days be beige.
self_questions: what ordinary day did you turn into an occasion?

rows.title: the hollow drum
rows.body: you have rhythm the way others have opinions. timing, music, the beat of a room, when to enter, when to drop the line, when to leave. and like a drum, your resonance comes from a hollow: a private emptiness that all the applause and plenty never quite fills. you make abundance look easy. the drum's secret is that it sounds fullest where it's most empty.
self_questions: what's the emptiness your rhythm is built around?
when do you feel genuinely full, not just successful?

rows.title: the rebel discount
rows.body: your excess is refusing things because they're conventional. some standard doors had genuinely good rooms behind them. contrarianism has a price tag too, and you've paid it a few times without checking the receipt.
self_questions: what did you skip just because everyone else was doing it?

rows.title: pride holds the door
rows.body: admitting you're hurt takes you longer than the hurting did. pride checks who's in the room first. only a few people have ever heard you say the words i'm not okay, and they know what it cost.
self_questions: what does it take for you to admit you're hurt?

rows.title: the easy leaver
rows.body: moving cities doesn't wound you. your airport goodbyes run shorter than everyone else's, and the guilt about that ran out years ago.
self_questions: what departure was easy for you that broke everyone else?

rows.title: harshness dims you
rows.body: cruel environments, pure transaction, weeks where nothing sacred gets any air. your light runs on meaning's oxygen, and harsh rooms have the windows painted shut.
self_questions: which room has the windows painted shut?

rows.title: useful or it doesn't stick
rows.body: knowledge earns its place in your head by having a job. trivia evaporates, application stays. you've forgotten whole subjects that had no handle to grab, and mastered dry ones the moment they became necessary.
self_questions: what did you learn only because you needed it?

rows.title: it leaks as the next big thing
